path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3402. Incompatible offices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3402. Incompatible offices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3402. Incompatible offices (2023)
content:
(a) No elected county officer shall at the same time serve as a member of the legislative
      body of any city, borough, town or township of any class, nor as school director of
      any school district, nor as a member of any board of health.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3407. Officers to secure funds, records, books, et cetera, from predecessors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3407. Officers to secure funds, records, books, et cetera, from predecessors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3407. Officers to secure funds, records, books, et cetera, from predecessors (2023)
content:
(a) Any person elected or appointed and duly commissioned to any county office shall
      demand and receive all records, books, drafts, plans, papers, seals or other official
      things, including all public funds, held in such office and not otherwise provided
      for by the act, approved the seventeenth day of May, one thousand nine hundred forty-nine
      (Pamphlet Laws 1403), known as the Municipal Unclaimed Moneys Act,1belonging to such office, from the person or persons who held the office immediately
      before his election or appointment, or from any other person or persons holding or
      possessing them.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3403. Oath of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3403. Oath of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3403. Oath of office (2023)
content:
(a) In addition to any oath or affirmation required by any other act of Assembly,
      all county officers, their deputies, assistants and clerks shall, before entering
      on the duties of their respective offices or employments, take and subscribe the following
      oath or affirmation:  “I do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will support, obey and
      defend the Constitution of the United States, and the Constitution of this Commonwealth,
      and that I will discharge the duties of my office (or employment) with fidelity; 
      that I have not paid or contributed, or promised to pay or contribute, either directly
      or indirectly, any money or other valuable thing to procure my nomination or election
      (or appointment), except for necessary and proper expenses expressly authorized by
      law;  that I have not knowingly violated any election law of this Commonwealth, or
      procured it to be done by others in my behalf;  that I will not knowingly receive,
      directly or indirectly, any money or other valuable thing for the performance or non-performance
      of any act or duty pertaining to my office (or employment), other than the compensation
      allowed by law.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3406. Records open to inspection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3406. Records open to inspection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3406. Records open to inspection (2023)
content:
(a) The minute book and other fiscal records and documents of the county may be open
      to the inspection of any taxpayer thereof, but the proper officers may make reasonable
      rules and regulations respecting the time of such inspection and fees for copying.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3404. Officers to have commissions recorded
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3404. Officers to have commissions recorded
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3404. Officers to have commissions recorded (2023)
content:
Every county officer receiving a commission from the Governor shall immediately deliver
   the same to the recorder of deeds for recordation, at the expense of such officer.  No such officer shall execute any of the duties of his office until he has so delivered
   the said commission.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3405. Offices, records and papers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3405. Offices, records and papers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3405. Offices, records and papers (2023)
content:
(a) Except as otherwise provided in subsection (a.1), the commissioners, controller,
      treasurer, sheriff, recorder of deeds, prothonotary, clerk of courts, clerk of the
      orphans' court, register of wills, recorder of deeds and district attorney shall keep
      their respective offices and all public records and papers belonging thereto at the
      county seat and in such buildings as may be erected or appropriated for such purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3409. Vacancies not otherwise provided for
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3409. Vacancies not otherwise provided for
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3409. Vacancies not otherwise provided for (2023)
content:
In case of a vacancy happening by death, resignation or otherwise in any county office
   created by the Constitution or laws of this Commonwealth, and where no other provision
   is made by the Constitution or by the provisions of this act to fill the vacancy,
   it shall be the duty of the Governor to appoint a suitable person to fill such office,
   who shall continue therein and discharge the duties thereof until the first Monday
   of January next succeeding the first municipal election which shall occur two or more
   months after the happening of such vacancy in counties of the second class.  In counties of the second class A the appointed person shall continue therein and
   discharge the duties thereof for the balance of the unexpired term.  Such appointee shall be confirmed by the Senate if in session.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3432. State associations authorized

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3408. Deputies to act in certain cases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3408. Deputies to act in certain cases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3408. Deputies to act in certain cases (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any county officer is authorized or required to appoint a deputy or deputies,
      such deputy, or principal deputy where there are more than one, shall, during the
      necessary or temporary absence of his principal, perform all the duties of such principal,
      and also, in case of a vacancy, until a successor is qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3412. Absconding officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3412. Absconding officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3412. Absconding officers (2023)
content:
The office of any county officer absconding from the county shall be vacant to all
   intents and purposes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article III. Fixing and Relocating Lines and Boundaries›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3306. Report of commissions; approval by court; certification of line
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article III. Fixing and Relocating Lines and Boundaries › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3306. Report of commissions; approval by court; certification of line
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3306. Report of commissions; approval by court; certification of line (2023)
content:
(a) The commission or a majority thereof shall make a report in writing and attach
      thereto a map or draft showing the courses and distances of the line ascertained and
      designated by them as the existing county line, or where they may have been directed
      to fix and determine a new county line, such map or draft, in lieu thereof, shall
      show the courses and distances of such new county line.  In either case, the map or draft shall also show the lands through which said line
      passes and the buildings in close proximity thereto, together with the roads and streams
      crossed by or near to such line.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3413. Qualifications of elected county officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3413. Qualifications of elected county officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3413. Qualifications of elected county officers (2023)
content:
No person shall be elected to any county office, except the office of district attorney
   otherwise provided for by this act, unless he shall be at least eighteen years of
   age, a citizen of the United States and a resident of the county, and shall have resided
   within the county for one year next preceding his election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3411. Penalty for neglect or refusal to perform duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3411. Penalty for neglect or refusal to perform duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3411. Penalty for neglect or refusal to perform duties (2023)
content:
If any county officer neglects or refuses to perform any duty imposed on him by the
   provisions of this act1or by the provisions of any other act of Assembly or by any rule of court or other
   provision of law, he shall, for each such neglect or refusal, be guilty of a misdemeanor,
   and, on conviction thereof, shall be sentenced to pay a fine not exceeding five hundred
   dollars ($500).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3433. Purpose; annual meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3433. Purpose; annual meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3433. Purpose; annual meetings (2023)
content:
(a) The purpose of the respective State associations shall be to discuss and resolve
      the various questions arising in the discharge of the duties and functions of the
      respective officers, and to provide uniform, efficient and economical methods of administering
      the affairs of the counties pertaining to their offices.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3410. County officials to furnish information to heads of the governmental departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3410. County officials to furnish information to heads of the governmental departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3410. County officials to furnish information to heads of the governmental departments (2023)
content:
(a) It shall be the duty of all county officers to furnish, on application thereof,
      to the head of any department of the State government, such information and copies
      of such records or documents contained in their respective offices as in the opinion
      of such head of department may be necessary or pertinent to the work of his respective
      department.  The county so furnishing information shall receive for copying and forwarding the
      same such reasonable compensation as the Auditor General may determine.  Such compensation shall be paid to the county by the State Treasurer out of moneys
      not otherwise appropriated, upon warrant from the Auditor General.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3434. Deputies and solicitors may attend annual meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3434. Deputies and solicitors may attend annual meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3434. Deputies and solicitors may attend annual meetings (2023)
content:
The deputy controller, the deputy sheriff, the deputy register of wills, the deputy
   treasurer, the deputy prothonotary, the deputy clerk of courts, the deputy recorder
   of deeds, the deputy clerk of orphans' court, the first assistant district attorney,
   one assistant public defender and the chief deputy coroner, with the approval of his
   principal and the solicitor for each office may attend the annual meetings of his
   respective associations, either together with the controller, sheriff, register of
   wills, prothonotary, clerk of courts, recorder of deeds, district attorney, public
   defender, coroner or treasurer, as the case may be, or in his place.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3437. Annual assessments for county commissioners, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3437. Annual assessments for county commissioners, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3437. Annual assessments for county commissioners, etc. (2023)
content:
(a) In addition to the expenses hereinbefore authorized, the necessary expenses of
      the association of county commissioners, county solicitors and chief clerks shall
      be apportioned among the counties holding membership in the association in amounts
      provided for by the rules and regulations of the association.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3436. Other meeting expenses paid by county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3436. Other meeting expenses paid by county
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3436. Other meeting expenses paid by county (2023)
content:
(a) In addition to the expenses hereinbefore authorized, the necessary expenses of
      the annual meetings of the associations hereinafter named, including printing, committee
      expenses and stenographical expense shall be paid in equal parts by the counties whose
      officers are members of the respective associations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(d) Removal of County Officers›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3450. Removal of county officers and appointees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (d) Removal of County Officers › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3450. Removal of county officers and appointees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3450. Removal of county officers and appointees (2023)
content:
(a) The county commissioners, the sheriffs, coroners, prothonotaries, registers of
      wills, recorders of deeds, treasurers, controllers, clerks of the courts, district
      attorneys, and any other officers of the county, whether elected or duly appointed
      to fill a vacancy, shall be removable from office only by impeachment, or by the Governor,
      for reasonable cause, after due notice and full hearing, on the advice of two-thirds
      of the Senate, or upon conviction of misbehavior in office or of any infamous crime,
      in accordance with the Constitution of this Commonwealth, but their title to office
      may be tried by proceedings of quo warranto as provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(f) Destruction of Valueless Records›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3470. Authority to destroy valueless records; approval of courts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (f) Destruction of Valueless Records › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3470. Authority to destroy valueless records; approval of courts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3470. Authority to destroy valueless records; approval of courts (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any officer of the county shall have an accumulation of records or other
      papers in his office which such officer shall deem valueless, he may destroy and dispose
      of the same, provided he shall have first obtained the approval of the court of common
      pleas, or of the orphans' court of the county in the case of the office of register
      of wills or clerk of the orphans' court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3435. Expenses of attending; members to be paid by county; time limit on meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3435. Expenses of attending; members to be paid by county; time limit on meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3435. Expenses of attending; members to be paid by county; time limit on meetings (2023)
content:
(a) The actual expenses of all authorized elected county officers attending the annual
      meetings of their associations shall be paid by the several counties out of the general
      county fund.  Each of these officers, except the county commissioners, shall be reimbursed for
      actual expenses not to exceed one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175) per day for
      the number of days specified in subsection (b) of this section, together with mileage
      going to and returning from such meeting and the registration fee.  The sum of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175) per day as set forth in this
      subsection shall be adjusted annually by the annual increase in the cost of living
      as determined annually by the United States Department of Labor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(e) Conduct of Official Business›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3460. Meetings open to public
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (e) Conduct of Official Business › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3460. Meetings open to public
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3460. Meetings open to public (2023)
content:
(a) All meetings, regular and special, of the board of county commissioners and of
      all boards, commissions and authorities, created by or operating as agencies of the
      county, are hereby declared to be public meetings, open to the public at all times.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(f) Destruction of Valueless Records›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3472. Petition to common pleas for order for destruction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (f) Destruction of Valueless Records › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3472. Petition to common pleas for order for destruction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3472. Petition to common pleas for order for destruction (2023)
content:
(a) Bonds of the county which have heretofore matured or may hereafter mature and
      all coupons pertaining to the same, upon redemption by the treasurer of the county,
      and all expired insurance policies on county property, both real and personal, which
      have been expired for a period of not less than six years, may be destroyed by incineration
      at a place to be designated by the county commissioners.  Before the destruction of any such public records, there shall first be filed a
      petition in the court of common pleas of the county, by either the county commissioners,
      the county controller or the county treasurer, or by all of them jointly, setting
      forth full and detailed information about the numbers, valuations and maturity dates
      of the bonds so to be destroyed, and full and detailed information in regard to the
      insurance policies, including the date of issuance, the name of the risk, the amount
      of the coverage, the date of expiration, and the disposition of any claim made in
      regard to said policy or policies so to be destroyed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IV. County Officers›(f) Destruction of Valueless Records›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3471. Destruction of retired public bonds and insurance policies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IV. County Officers › (f) Destruction of Valueless Records › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3471. Destruction of retired public bonds and insurance policies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3471. Destruction of retired public bonds and insurance policies (2023)
content:
The county commissioners are hereby authorized and empowered to destroy by incineration,
   under the terms and conditions hereinafter provided, retired public bonds and coupons,
   whether serial or otherwise, and expired insurance policies on county property.

      treasurer, sheriff, recorder of deeds, prothonotary, clerk of courts, clerk of the
      orphans' court, register of wills, recorder of deeds and district attorney shall keep
      their respective offices and all public records and papers belonging thereto at the
      county seat and in such buildings as may be erected or appropriated for such purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3407. Officers to secure funds, records, books, et cetera, from predecessors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3407. Officers to secure funds, records, books, et cetera, from predecessors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3407. Officers to secure funds, records, books, et cetera, from predecessors (2023)
content:
(a) Any person elected or appointed and duly commissioned to any county office shall
      demand and receive all records, books, drafts, plans, papers, seals or other official
      things, including all public funds, held in such office and not otherwise provided
      for by the act, approved the seventeenth day of May, one thousand nine hundred forty-nine
      (Pamphlet Laws 1403), known as the Municipal Unclaimed Moneys Act,1belonging to such office, from the person or persons who held the office immediately
      before his election or appointment, or from any other person or persons holding or
      possessing them.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3406. Records open to inspection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3406. Records open to inspection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3406. Records open to inspection (2023)
content:
(a) The minute book and other fiscal records and documents of the county may be open
      to the inspection of any taxpayer thereof, but the proper officers may make reasonable
      rules and regulations respecting the time of such inspection and fees for copying.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3409. Vacancies not otherwise provided for
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3409. Vacancies not otherwise provided for
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3409. Vacancies not otherwise provided for (2023)
content:
In case of a vacancy happening by death, resignation or otherwise in any county office
   created by the Constitution or laws of this Commonwealth, and where no other provision
   is made by the Constitution or by the provisions of this act to fill the vacancy,
   it shall be the duty of the Governor to appoint a suitable person to fill such office,
   who shall continue therein and discharge the duties thereof until the first Monday
   of January next succeeding the first municipal election which shall occur two or more
   months after the happening of such vacancy in counties of the second class.  In counties of the second class A the appointed person shall continue therein and
   discharge the duties thereof for the balance of the unexpired term.  Such appointee shall be confirmed by the Senate if in session.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3410. County officials to furnish information to heads of the governmental departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3410. County officials to furnish information to heads of the governmental departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3410. County officials to furnish information to heads of the governmental departments (2023)
content:
(a) It shall be the duty of all county officers to furnish, on application thereof,
      to the head of any department of the State government, such information and copies
      of such records or documents contained in their respective offices as in the opinion
      of such head of department may be necessary or pertinent to the work of his respective
      department.  The county so furnishing information shall receive for copying and forwarding the
      same such reasonable compensation as the Auditor General may determine.  Such compensation shall be paid to the county by the State Treasurer out of moneys
      not otherwise appropriated, upon warrant from the Auditor General.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3411. Penalty for neglect or refusal to perform duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3411. Penalty for neglect or refusal to perform duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3411. Penalty for neglect or refusal to perform duties (2023)
content:
If any county officer neglects or refuses to perform any duty imposed on him by the
   provisions of this act1or by the provisions of any other act of Assembly or by any rule of court or other
   provision of law, he shall, for each such neglect or refusal, be guilty of a misdemeanor,
   and, on conviction thereof, shall be sentenced to pay a fine not exceeding five hundred
   dollars ($500).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(d) Removal of County Officers›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3450. Removal of county officers and appointees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (d) Removal of County Officers › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3450. Removal of county officers and appointees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3450. Removal of county officers and appointees (2023)
content:
(a) The county commissioners, the sheriffs, coroners, prothonotaries, registers of
      wills, recorders of deeds, treasurers, controllers, clerks of the courts, district
      attorneys, and any other officers of the county, whether elected or duly appointed
      to fill a vacancy, shall be removable from office only by impeachment, or by the Governor,
      for reasonable cause, after due notice and full hearing, on the advice of two-thirds
      of the Senate, or upon conviction of misbehavior in office or of any infamous crime,
      in accordance with the Constitution of this Commonwealth, but their title to office
      may be tried by proceedings of quo warranto as provided by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3412. Absconding officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3412. Absconding officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3412. Absconding officers (2023)
content:
The office of any county officer absconding from the county shall be vacant to all
   intents and purposes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3432. State associations authorized
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3432. State associations authorized
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3432. State associations authorized (2023)
content:
County officers of the county may join with county officers of other counties of the
   Commonwealth and organize a State association, as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3408. Deputies to act in certain cases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3408. Deputies to act in certain cases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3408. Deputies to act in certain cases (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any county officer is authorized or required to appoint a deputy or deputies,
      such deputy, or principal deputy where there are more than one, shall, during the
      necessary or temporary absence of his principal, perform all the duties of such principal,
      and also, in case of a vacancy, until a successor is qualified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3413. Qualifications of elected county officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3413. Qualifications of elected county officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3413. Qualifications of elected county officers (2023)
content:
No person shall be elected to any county office, except the office of district attorney
   otherwise provided for by this act, unless he shall be at least eighteen years of
   age, a citizen of the United States and a resident of the county, and shall have resided
   within the county for one year next preceding his election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(f) Destruction of Valueless Records›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3470. Authority to destroy valueless records; approval of courts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (f) Destruction of Valueless Records › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3470. Authority to destroy valueless records; approval of courts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3470. Authority to destroy valueless records; approval of courts (2023)
content:
(a) Whenever any officer of the county shall have an accumulation of records or other
      papers in his office which such officer shall deem valueless, he may destroy and dispose
      of the same, provided he shall have first obtained the approval of the court of common
      pleas, or of the orphans' court of the county in the case of the office of register
      of wills or clerk of the orphans' court.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3433. Purpose; annual meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3433. Purpose; annual meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3433. Purpose; annual meetings (2023)
content:
(a) The purpose of the respective State associations shall be to discuss and resolve
      the various questions arising in the discharge of the duties and functions of the
      respective officers, and to provide uniform, efficient and economical methods of administering
      the affairs of the counties pertaining to their offices.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3437. Annual assessments for county commissioners, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3437. Annual assessments for county commissioners, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3437. Annual assessments for county commissioners, etc. (2023)
content:
(a) In addition to the expenses hereinbefore authorized, the necessary expenses of
      the association of county commissioners, county solicitors and chief clerks shall
      be apportioned among the counties holding membership in the association in amounts
      provided for by the rules and regulations of the association.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3436. Other meeting expenses paid by county
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3436. Other meeting expenses paid by county
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3436. Other meeting expenses paid by county (2023)
content:
(a) In addition to the expenses hereinbefore authorized, the necessary expenses of
      the annual meetings of the associations hereinafter named, including printing, committee
      expenses and stenographical expense shall be paid in equal parts by the counties whose
      officers are members of the respective associations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3434. Deputies and solicitors may attend annual meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3434. Deputies and solicitors may attend annual meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3434. Deputies and solicitors may attend annual meetings (2023)
content:
The deputy controller, the deputy sheriff, the deputy register of wills, the deputy
   treasurer, the deputy prothonotary, the deputy clerk of courts, the deputy recorder
   of deeds, the deputy clerk of orphans' court, the first assistant district attorney,
   one assistant public defender and the chief deputy coroner, with the approval of his
   principal and the solicitor for each office may attend the annual meetings of his
   respective associations, either together with the controller, sheriff, register of
   wills, prothonotary, clerk of courts, recorder of deeds, district attorney, public
   defender, coroner or treasurer, as the case may be, or in his place.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(c) State Associations›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3435. Expenses of attending; members to be paid by county; time limit on meetings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (c) State Associations › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3435. Expenses of attending; members to be paid by county; time limit on meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3435. Expenses of attending; members to be paid by county; time limit on meetings (2023)
content:
(a) The actual expenses of all authorized elected county officers attending the annual
      meetings of their associations shall be paid by the several counties out of the general
      county fund.  Each of these officers, except the county commissioners, shall be reimbursed for
      actual expenses not to exceed one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175) per day for
      the number of days specified in subsection (b) of this section, together with mileage
      going to and returning from such meeting and the registration fee.  The sum of one hundred seventy-five dollars ($175) per day as set forth in this
      subsection shall be adjusted annually by the annual increase in the cost of living
      as determined annually by the United States Department of Labor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501. Election; vacancies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501. Election; vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501. Election; vacancies (2023)
content:
(a) Three county commissioners shall be elected in the county in the year one thousand
      nine hundred and fifty-five and every fourth year thereafter.  In the election of commissioners, each qualified elector shall vote for no more
      than two persons.  The three persons having the highest number of votes shall be elected.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(f) Destruction of Valueless Records›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3471. Destruction of retired public bonds and insurance policies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (f) Destruction of Valueless Records › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3471. Destruction of retired public bonds and insurance policies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3471. Destruction of retired public bonds and insurance policies (2023)
content:
The county commissioners are hereby authorized and empowered to destroy by incineration,
   under the terms and conditions hereinafter provided, retired public bonds and coupons,
   whether serial or otherwise, and expired insurance policies on county property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(e) Conduct of Official Business›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3460. Meetings open to public
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (e) Conduct of Official Business › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3460. Meetings open to public
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3460. Meetings open to public (2023)
content:
(a) All meetings, regular and special, of the board of county commissioners and of
      all boards, commissions and authorities, created by or operating as agencies of the
      county, are hereby declared to be public meetings, open to the public at all times.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(f) Destruction of Valueless Records›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3472. Petition to common pleas for order for destruction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (f) Destruction of Valueless Records › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3472. Petition to common pleas for order for destruction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3472. Petition to common pleas for order for destruction (2023)
content:
(a) Bonds of the county which have heretofore matured or may hereafter mature and
      all coupons pertaining to the same, upon redemption by the treasurer of the county,
      and all expired insurance policies on county property, both real and personal, which
      have been expired for a period of not less than six years, may be destroyed by incineration
      at a place to be designated by the county commissioners.  Before the destruction of any such public records, there shall first be filed a
      petition in the court of common pleas of the county, by either the county commissioners,
      the county controller or the county treasurer, or by all of them jointly, setting
      forth full and detailed information about the numbers, valuations and maturity dates
      of the bonds so to be destroyed, and full and detailed information in regard to the
      insurance policies, including the date of issuance, the name of the risk, the amount
      of the coverage, the date of expiration, and the disposition of any claim made in
      regard to said policy or policies so to be destroyed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3505. Power to administer oaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3505. Power to administer oaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3505. Power to administer oaths (2023)
content:
The commissioners shall respectively have power to administer oaths and affirmations
   in all cases arising in the performance of the duties of their office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3506. Expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3506. Expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3506. Expenses (2023)
content:
The county commissioners shall be allowed their expenses necessarily incurred and
   actually paid in the discharge of their official duties or in the performance of any
   service, office or duty imposed upon county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3504. Certified copies of proceedings to be evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3504. Certified copies of proceedings to be evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3504. Certified copies of proceedings to be evidence (2023)
content:
Copies of the proceedings of the commissioners and of all records in their possession,
   certified by their chief clerk under the county seal, shall be admitted in evidence
   in any of the courts of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3507. Office furniture, stationery, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3507. Office furniture, stationery, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3507. Office furniture, stationery, etc. (2023)
content:
(a) The county commissioners, at the cost of the county, shall purchase and provide
      the office furniture, equipment and supplies, blank books, blanks, dockets, books
      for records, stationery, postage, fuel, light and janitor and telephone service required
      for each of the county officers whose offices are located in the county buildings
      or at such other places at the county seat as may be designated by the commissioners,
      and all supplies used by the public in connection with such offices.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3503. Quorum; execution of official instruments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3503. Quorum; execution of official instruments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3503. Quorum; execution of official instruments (2023)
content:
(a) The commissioners shall constitute a board, two members of which shall be a quorum
      for the transaction of business, and when convened in pursuance of notice or according
      to adjournment shall be competent to perform all the duties appertaining to the office
      of county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3502. Organization
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3502. Organization
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3502. Organization (2023)
content:
The county commissioners shall meet on the first Monday of January in the year one
   thousand nine hundred and fifty-six and on the first Monday of January every fourth
   year thereafter, in the office provided for them at the county seat, for the purpose
   of organization.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501. Election; vacancies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501. Election; vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501. Election; vacancies (2023)
content:
(a) Three county commissioners shall be elected in the county in the year one thousand
      nine hundred and fifty-five and every fourth year thereafter.  In the election of commissioners, each qualified elector shall vote for no more
      than two persons.  The three persons having the highest number of votes shall be elected.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3509. Take money and property by gift, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3509. Take money and property by gift, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3509. Take money and property by gift, etc. (2023)
content:
The county commissioners may take by gift, grant, devise or bequest, any money or
   property, real, personal or mixed, in trust for the benefit of the county, and the
   care and management, investment, sale, reinvestment and disposal of such trust funds
   or property shall be vested in the sinking fund commission and shall be governed thereby,
   subject to such direction as the donors of such funds and property may prescribe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(b) Chief Clerk of County Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3521. Duties and powers of chief clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (b) Chief Clerk of County Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3521. Duties and powers of chief clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3521. Duties and powers of chief clerk (2023)
content:
(a) The chief clerk shall keep the books and accounts of the board of county commissioners,
      record and file their proceedings and papers, attest all orders and warrants issued
      by them, and perform all other duties pertaining to his office as chief clerk.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3508. Ordinances and resolutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3508. Ordinances and resolutions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3508. Ordinances and resolutions (2023)
content:
(a) The board of commissioners may adopt resolutions and ordinances prescribing the
      manner in which powers of the county shall be carried out and generally regulating
      the affairs of the county.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3510. Creation of capital reserve fund for anticipated capital expenditures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3510. Creation of capital reserve fund for anticipated capital expenditures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3510. Creation of capital reserve fund for anticipated capital expenditures (2023)
content:
The county commissioners shall have the power to create and maintain a separate capital
   reserve fund for anticipated legal capital expenditures.  The money in the fund shall be used from time to time for the construction, purchase
   or replacement of or addition to county buildings, equipment, machinery, motor vehicles
   or other capital assets of the county and for no other purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(b) Chief Clerk of County Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3520. Chief clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (b) Chief Clerk of County Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3520. Chief clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3520. Chief clerk (2023)
content: The county commissioners shall appoint a chief clerk.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3504. Certified copies of proceedings to be evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3504. Certified copies of proceedings to be evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3504. Certified copies of proceedings to be evidence (2023)
content:
Copies of the proceedings of the commissioners and of all records in their possession,
   certified by their chief clerk under the county seal, shall be admitted in evidence
   in any of the courts of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3502. Organization
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3502. Organization
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3502. Organization (2023)
content:
The county commissioners shall meet on the first Monday of January in the year one
   thousand nine hundred and fifty-six and on the first Monday of January every fourth
   year thereafter, in the office provided for them at the county seat, for the purpose
   of organization.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3508. Ordinances and resolutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3508. Ordinances and resolutions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3508. Ordinances and resolutions (2023)
content:
(a) The board of commissioners may adopt resolutions and ordinances prescribing the
      manner in which powers of the county shall be carried out and generally regulating
      the affairs of the county.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3510. Creation of capital reserve fund for anticipated capital expenditures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3510. Creation of capital reserve fund for anticipated capital expenditures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3510. Creation of capital reserve fund for anticipated capital expenditures (2023)
content:
The county commissioners shall have the power to create and maintain a separate capital
   reserve fund for anticipated legal capital expenditures.  The money in the fund shall be used from time to time for the construction, purchase
   or replacement of or addition to county buildings, equipment, machinery, motor vehicles
   or other capital assets of the county and for no other purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3507. Office furniture, stationery, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3507. Office furniture, stationery, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3507. Office furniture, stationery, etc. (2023)
content:
(a) The county commissioners, at the cost of the county, shall purchase and provide
      the office furniture, equipment and supplies, blank books, blanks, dockets, books
      for records, stationery, postage, fuel, light and janitor and telephone service required
      for each of the county officers whose offices are located in the county buildings
      or at such other places at the county seat as may be designated by the commissioners,
      and all supplies used by the public in connection with such offices.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3509. Take money and property by gift, etc.
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3509. Take money and property by gift, etc.
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3509. Take money and property by gift, etc. (2023)
content:
The county commissioners may take by gift, grant, devise or bequest, any money or
   property, real, personal or mixed, in trust for the benefit of the county, and the
   care and management, investment, sale, reinvestment and disposal of such trust funds
   or property shall be vested in the sinking fund commission and shall be governed thereby,
   subject to such direction as the donors of such funds and property may prescribe.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3511. Operating reserve fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V. County Commissioners and Chief Clerk › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3511. Operating reserve fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3511. Operating reserve fund (2023)
content:
(a) The county commissioners shall have the power to create and maintain a separate
      operating reserve fund in order to minimize future revenue shortfalls and deficits,
      provide greater continuity and predictability in the funding of vital government services,
      minimize the need to increase taxes to balance the budget in times of fiscal distress,
      provide the capacity to undertake long-range financial planning and develop fiscal
      resources to meet long-term needs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3506. Expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3506. Expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3506. Expenses (2023)
content:
The county commissioners shall be allowed their expenses necessarily incurred and
   actually paid in the discharge of their official duties or in the performance of any
   service, office or duty imposed upon county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3503. Quorum; execution of official instruments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3503. Quorum; execution of official instruments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3503. Quorum; execution of official instruments (2023)
content:
(a) The commissioners shall constitute a board, two members of which shall be a quorum
      for the transaction of business, and when convened in pursuance of notice or according
      to adjournment shall be competent to perform all the duties appertaining to the office
      of county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3505. Power to administer oaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3505. Power to administer oaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3505. Power to administer oaths (2023)
content:
The commissioners shall respectively have power to administer oaths and affirmations
   in all cases arising in the performance of the duties of their office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Chief Clerk of County Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3521. Duties and powers of chief clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Chief Clerk of County Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3521. Duties and powers of chief clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3521. Duties and powers of chief clerk (2023)
content:
(a) The chief clerk shall keep the books and accounts of the board of county commissioners,
      record and file their proceedings and papers, attest all orders and warrants issued
      by them, and perform all other duties pertaining to his office as chief clerk.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(a) Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3511. Operating reserve fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (a) Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3511. Operating reserve fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3511. Operating reserve fund (2023)
content:
(a) The county commissioners shall have the power to create and maintain a separate
      operating reserve fund in order to minimize future revenue shortfalls and deficits,
      provide greater continuity and predictability in the funding of vital government services,
      minimize the need to increase taxes to balance the budget in times of fiscal distress,
      provide the capacity to undertake long-range financial planning and develop fiscal
      resources to meet long-term needs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article V-A. Civil Service›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501-A. Civil service for certain employes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article V-A. Civil Service › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501-A. Civil service for certain employes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3501-A. Civil service for certain employes (2023)
content:
The county commissioners are hereby authorized to establish by ordinance, a merit
   system for the selection, tenure, promotion and discharge of employes involved in
   any work for which the county receives or is eligible to receive Federal or State
   grants-in-aid.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VI. Controller›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3602. Eligibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VI. Controller › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3602. Eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3602. Eligibility (2023)
content:
(a) No person holding office under the United States shall be eligible to the office
      of county controller during his continuance in such office nor until one year thereafter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VI. Controller›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3601. Election and term; seal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VI. Controller › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3601. Election and term; seal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3601. Election and term; seal (2023)
content:
(a) At the municipal election immediately preceding the expiration of the term of
      the controller now in office and quadrennially thereafter, the qualified electors
      of the county shall elect one citizen of the county, who shall serve as controller
      for the term of four years from the first Monday of January following his election
      or until his successor shall be qualified, if he so long shall behave himself well.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VI. Controller›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3605. Expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VI. Controller › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3605. Expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3605. Expenses (2023)
content:
The county controller and his deputy clerks and employees shall be allowed their expenses
   necessarily incurred and actually paid in the discharge of their official duties or
   in the performance of any service or duty imposed upon them.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VI. Controller›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3603. Deputy controller and clerks
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VI. Controller › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3603. Deputy controller and clerks
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3603. Deputy controller and clerks (2023)
content:
The controller shall appoint a deputy controller and clerks, and may authorize one
   or more of the clerks employed in his office to administer to all persons oaths and
   affirmations pertaining to the business of the office, with the same force and effect
   as if administered by the controller or deputy controller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›(b) Chief Clerk of County Commissioners›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3520. Chief clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › (b) Chief Clerk of County Commissioners › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3520. Chief clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3520. Chief clerk (2023)
content: The county commissioners shall appoint a chief clerk.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VII. Lot and Block System›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3705. Putting system into effect
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VII. Lot and Block System › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3705. Putting system into effect
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3705. Putting system into effect (2023)
content:
Where the commissioners have established the lot and block system in the office of
   the county controller, and where the county controller has certified to the commissioners
   that said system has been completely installed in either the whole of the county or
   completely installed in one or more municipal subdivisions thereof, then the commissioners
   shall proceed to put said system into effect in the manner hereinafter set forth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VII. Lot and Block System›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3707. Effect of order; correction of assessments; recording instruments; tax bills; liens; tax sales
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VII. Lot and Block System › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3707. Effect of order; correction of assessments; recording instruments; tax bills; liens; tax sales
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3707. Effect of order; correction of assessments; recording instruments; tax bills; liens; tax sales (2023)
content: The effect of the order of the Court of Common Pleas shall be as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VI. Controller›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3604. Solicitor to the controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VI. Controller › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3604. Solicitor to the controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3604. Solicitor to the controller (2023)
content:
The county controller may designate and appoint one person learned in the law to act
   as his solicitor.  Such solicitor shall advise upon all such legal matters as may be submitted to him
   and shall conduct any litigation desired by the county controller.  He shall hold office at the pleasure of the controller.  He shall receive such salary as may be fixed by the salary board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VII. Lot and Block System›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3702. Systems which may be adopted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VII. Lot and Block System › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3702. Systems which may be adopted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3702. Systems which may be adopted (2023)
content:
In establishing the said lot and block system, the commissioners may adopt any system
   covered by such designation, now in use either in municipalities in the Commonwealth
   or in use in the municipalities in other states, or a combination of such systems,
   as they shall deem proper, in order to supply the needs of said county.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VII. Lot and Block System›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3706. Petition to common pleas; determination; order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VII. Lot and Block System › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3706. Petition to common pleas; determination; order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3706. Petition to common pleas; determination; order (2023)
content:
Immediately upon the receipt of the certification of completion from the county controller,
   the commissioners shall present their petition to the Court of Common Pleas, setting
   forth the establishment of such lot and block system, the fact of its completion,
   either in the county as a whole or within one or more municipal subdivisions, and
   a brief statement describing the method of operation of the lot and block system so
   established.  If the court shall determine that the said system has been established in accordance
   with the provisions of this article and has been completed, it shall make an order
   placing the same in effect as of the first Monday of January next succeeding such
   order.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VII. Lot and Block System›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3704. Part of system transferred to deed registry office, part maintained in office of controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VII. Lot and Block System › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3704. Part of system transferred to deed registry office, part maintained in office of controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3704. Part of system transferred to deed registry office, part maintained in office of controller (2023)
content:
When installation of the lot and block system has been completed, the division of
   said system having custody of the plats and plat books and the upkeep of the same
   shall be transferred to the deed registry office of said county, and the files, cards,
   indexes and records relating to the liening of county taxes shall remain in and be
   maintained by the office of the controller of said county.  The deed registrar and the controller of the county are hereby charged with and
   required to operate and maintain the several portions of the lot and block system
   placed in their custody, as herein provided.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VII. Lot and Block System›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3701. County commissioners to establish
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VII. Lot and Block System › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3701. County commissioners to establish
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3701. County commissioners to establish (2023)
content:
The county commissioners are hereby empowered to establish, in the office of the county
   controller, the lot and block system for the registration of land titles, for the
   accumulation of county tax liens, and for the enumeration of the parcels of real estate
   to be assessed for county, city, borough, township, school and institution district
   taxation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VII. Lot and Block System›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3703. Cost and expense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VII. Lot and Block System › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3703. Cost and expense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3703. Cost and expense (2023)
content:
For the purpose of defraying the cost and expense of establishing said lot and block
   system, the commissioners may use current tax revenue or may issue general obligation
   bonds in such amounts as are necessary and in such manner as provided by the Municipal
   Borrowing Law.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VIII. Treasurer›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3805. Misapplication of funds collected for specific purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VIII. Treasurer › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3805. Misapplication of funds collected for specific purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3805. Misapplication of funds collected for specific purposes (2023)
content:
Whenever any moneys are collected by law in any county for any special purpose and
   paid into the hands of the treasurer of the county, it shall be unlawful for such
   treasurer to apply such moneys or any part thereof to any other purpose than that
   for which such moneys were collected.  Every such misapplication shall be a misdemeanor, upon conviction whereof the treasurer
   shall be punished by a fine of not less than the amount so misapplied and by imprisonment
   for not less than three months nor more than one year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VII. Lot and Block System›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3708. Registration of ownership of property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VII. Lot and Block System › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3708. Registration of ownership of property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3708. Registration of ownership of property (2023)
content:
(a) All persons, corporations, municipal corporations, authorities, districts or political
      subdivisions, hereafter acquiring any interest in real estate, whether by purchase,
      gift, devise, inheritance, order of court, treasurer's sale, sheriff's sale, judicial
      sale, eminent domain or otherwise, shall register in the office of the county commissioners
      their deeds, resolutions, orders of court or other evidence of title, so that the
      same may be endorsed in accordance with the act of May 2, 1899 (P.L. 162).1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IX. County Solicitor›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3904. Assistant solicitors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IX. County Solicitor › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3904. Assistant solicitors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3904. Assistant solicitors (2023)
content:
The county solicitor may, with the consent of the county commissioners, appoint, to
   assist him in the discharge of the duties of his office, assistant county solicitors
   and special counsel, who shall be attorneys-at-law admitted to practice in the courts
   of this Commonwealth.  Each assistant and special counsel shall perform such duties in connection with
   the legal affairs of the county as may be assigned to him by the county commissioners
   or the county solicitor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article IX. County Solicitor›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3902. Duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article IX. County Solicitor › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3902. Duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3902. Duties (2023)
content:
He shall commence and prosecute all suits brought or to be brought by the county wherein
   or whereby any rights, privileges, properties, claims or demands of the county are
   involved, as well as defend all actions or suits brought against the county, and shall
   perform all duties now enjoined by law upon county solicitors, and shall do all and
   every professional act and render legal advice incident to the office, which may be
   required of him by the commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article VIII. Treasurer›PA ST 16 P.S. § 3807. Solicitor to county treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article VIII. Treasurer › PA ST 16 P.S. § 3807. Solicitor to county treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 3807. Solicitor to county treasurer (2023)
content:
The county treasurer is hereby authorized to appoint one person, learned in the law,
   as his solicitor.  The solicitor shall advise upon all legal matters that may be submitted to him and
   shall conduct any litigation when requested so to do by the treasurer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4202. Sheriff may act by deputy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4202. Sheriff may act by deputy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4202. Sheriff may act by deputy (2023)
content:
Whenever the sheriff is or shall be required by law to act in person under or by virtue
   of any writ or process whatsoever issued by the courts of this Commonwealth, he may
   act either in person or by a regularly appointed deputy sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 2. Second Class County Code›Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner›(a) Sheriff›PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203.1. Chief deputy in counties of the second class
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 2. Second Class County Code › Article XII. Sheriff and Coroner › (a) Sheriff › PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203.1. Chief deputy in counties of the second class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 4203.1. Chief deputy in counties of the second class (2023)
content:
In counties of the second class, the sheriff of the county shall appoint in accordance
   with section 1216,1by commission duly recorded in the Department of Real Estate, a chief deputy, whose
