title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties › Article XV. General Salary Provisions › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 11001. Salaries to be altered only by act of assembly, notwithstanding change in population
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 11001. Salaries to be altered only by act of assembly, notwithstanding change in population (2023)
content:
The schedule of salaries fixed by this act,1and the act2to which this is a supplement, shall not be altered or changed by the increase or
   decrease of the population of the county, as shown by any national census, but the
   same shall be and remain as fixed by law, notwithstanding such increase or decrease
   of population, until altered by act of assembly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties›Article XV. General Salary Provisions›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-5.1. District attorneys; salaries

(a) The district attorney of a city and county of the first class shall be compensated
      at one thousand dollars ($1,000) lower than the compensation paid to a judge of a
      court of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties›Article XV. General Salary Provisions›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-13. Severability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties › Article XV. General Salary Provisions › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-13. Severability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-13. Severability (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act shall be severable.  If any word, phrase, clause, sentence, section or provision of this act is for any
   reason held to be unconstitutional, the decision of the court shall not affect or
   impair any of the remaining provisions of this act.  It is hereby declared as the legislative intent that this act would have been adopted
   had such unconstitutional word, phrase, clause, sentence, section or provision thereof
   not been included herein.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties›Article XV. General Salary Provisions›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-12. Limitations on payments

      this restriction shall not apply to those county officers receiving a salary as executive
      and administrative officers of institution districts existing in their counties.

(a) From and after the effective date of this section, the county commissioners shall

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties › Article XV. General Salary Provisions › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-11. Multiple officeholders; salaries

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties›Article XV. General Salary Provisions›(b) Counties of the Third Class›PA ST 16 P.S. § 11023. Salaries of jury commissioners

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties › Article XV. General Salary Provisions › (d) Counties of the Fifth Class › PA ST 16 P.S. § 11072. Additional compensation of coroner for over 100 inquests
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 11072. Additional compensation of coroner for over 100 inquests (2023)
content:
In counties of the fifth class, the coroner shall receive the sum of twenty-five dollars
   ($25) for each inquest held by him after he has held one hundred inquests during each
   year.  Such moneys shall be paid by the county and shall be in addition to the salary payable
   under existing law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties›Article XV. General Salary Provisions›(e) Counties of the Sixth Class›PA ST 16 P.S. § 11101. Jury commissioners; compensation and mileage
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties › Article XV. General Salary Provisions › (e) Counties of the Sixth Class › PA ST 16 P.S. § 11101. Jury commissioners; compensation and mileage
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 11101. Jury commissioners; compensation and mileage (2023)
content:
Hereafter the compensation of the jury commissioners in counties of the sixth class
   shall be six dollars per diem for each and every day, not exceeding sixty-five days
   in any year, necessarily employed in the discharge of their duties, together with
   six cents per mile circular from and to their homes once each and every week so employed.

content:

   thousand dollars, payable from the county treasury in the manner fixed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties›Article XV. General Salary Provisions›(e) Counties of the Sixth Class›PA ST 16 P.S. § 11103. Counties of sixth class; autopsies; cost limited

content:

   of the county.

   of population, until altered by act of assembly.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-11. Multiple officeholders; salaries (2023)
content:

   a salary is herein fixed, he shall receive the highest salary fixed for any one of
   the offices which he holds, plus an additional amount of two thousand dollars ($2,000)
   per annum.  The periodic salary increases provided for in section 10.11of this act shall be applicable to this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 P.S. Counties›Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties›(a) General Provisions›PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-13. Severability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 P.S. Counties › Chapter 4. Other Provisions Concerning Counties › (a) General Provisions › PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-13. Severability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 P.S. § 11011-13. Severability (2023)
content:
The provisions of this act shall be severable.  If any word, phrase, clause, sentence, section or provision of this act is for any
   reason held to be unconstitutional, the decision of the court shall not affect or
   impair any of the remaining provisions of this act.  It is hereby declared as the legislative intent that this act would have been adopted
   had such unconstitutional word, phrase, clause, sentence, section or provision thereof
   not been included herein.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 1. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 108. Legislation according to class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 108. Legislation according to class (2023)
content:

   to each county, or to particular classes, as fixed and appointed by this title.  Each law adopted by the General Assembly for one or more of the classes fixed and
   appointed by this title shall be deemed to be general laws.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 311. Ascertainment, certification and effect of change of class (2023)
content:
(a) Ascertainment.--The classification of counties shall be ascertained and fixed according to population
      by reference to the Federal decennial census under this section, less the number of
      individuals residing on lands that have been ceded to the United States.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 1. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 105. Holding of office

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 105. Holding of office (2023)
content:
An individual holding an elective office under the County Code shall continue to hold
   the office until the expiration of the individual's term, subject to the conditions
   and salary attached to the office prior to October 24, 2018.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 1. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 104. Saving clause
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 1. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 104. Saving clause
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 104. Saving clause (2023)
content:
(a) Continuation.--This title, as far as the provisions of this title are the same as the provisions
      of laws in existence on January 1, 1956, shall be construed as a continuation of the
      laws and not as a new enactment.  The repeal by the County Code of any provisions of law may not revive any law repealed
      or superseded prior to January 1, 1956, nor affect the existence or class of any county
      created prior to January 1, 1956.  This title may not affect any act done, liability incurred or right accrued or vested,
      nor affect any suit or prosecution, pending or to be instituted, to enforce any right
      or penalty or punish any offense under the authority of the repealed laws.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 311. Ascertainment, certification and effect of change of class (2023)
content:
(a) Ascertainment.--The classification of counties shall be ascertained and fixed according to population
      by reference to the Federal decennial census under this section, less the number of
      individuals residing on lands that have been ceded to the United States.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 301. Enumeration of counties (2023)
content:

   Clinton, Columbia, Crawford, Cumberland, Dauphin, Delaware, Elk, Erie, Fayette, Forest,
   Franklin, Fulton, Greene, Huntingdon, Indiana, Jefferson, Juniata, Lackawanna, Lancaster,
   Lawrence, Lebanon, Lehigh, Luzerne, Lycoming, McKean, Mercer, Mifflin, Monroe, Montgomery,
   Montour, Northampton, Northumberland, Perry, Philadelphia, Pike, Potter, Schuylkill,
   Snyder, Somerset, Sullivan, Susquehanna, Tioga, Union, Venango, Warren, Washington,
   Wayne, Westmoreland, Wyoming and York.

      affected by the question and not adjoining any of the counties involved to act in

content:

      502 (relating to Commonwealth Court designation of neutral court and appointment of

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part II. Counties of the First Class › Chapter 23. Vehicle Rental Tax › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 2301. Authorization of vehicle rental tax by counties of the first class
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 2301. Authorization of vehicle rental tax by counties of the first class (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization.--Notwithstanding any provision of this title or any other law, each county of the first
      class may impose an excise tax on the rental of a rental vehicle in that county.  If the county is coterminous with a city of the first class, imposition of the tax
      in the county, if any, shall be by the city.  The tax may be imposed on a person renting a rental vehicle at a rate of up to 2%
      of the purchase price of the rental.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 121. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12103. Proceedings for recovery of penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 121. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12103. Proceedings for recovery of penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12103. Proceedings for recovery of penalties (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise specifically provided in this part, if a pecuniary penalty or forfeiture
   is imposed by this part, the proceeding for the recovery of the pecuniary penalty
   or forfeiture shall be by indictment in the court of common pleas or by civil action
   as debts of equivalent amount are by law recoverable.  Magisterial district judges may not have jurisdiction of a suit or action for the
   recovery of a penalty imposed by this part for official misconduct.  The suit or action, if brought in the court of common pleas, shall have preference
   for trial over all other actions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 121. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12104. Collection of tax and municipal claims by suit and limitations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 121. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12104. Collection of tax and municipal claims by suit and limitations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12104. Collection of tax and municipal claims by suit and limitations (2023)
content:
(a) Proceedings.--In addition to the remedies provided by law for the collection of tax and municipal
      claims, a county may proceed for the recovery and collection of a tax or municipal
      claim owed to the county against each owner of the property owing the tax or municipal
      claim to the county by a civil action or other appropriate remedy.  A penalty of 10% and interest at the prevailing legal rate and costs of suit shall
      be added to each judgment obtained for the taxes or municipal claim.  Upon judgment, execution may be issued without a stay or benefit of an exemption
      law.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 5. Fixing and Relocating Lines and Boundaries › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Report of boundary commission, approval by court and certification of line
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 506. Report of boundary commission, approval by court and certification of line (2023)
content:
(a) Report.--The boundary commission shall prepare a written report containing a map or draft showing
      the courses and distances of the line ascertained and designated by the commission
      as the existing county line, or if the commission has been directed to fix and determine
      a new county line, the map or draft shall instead show the courses and distances of
      the new county line.  A map or draft under this subsection shall show the lands through which the line
      passes and the buildings in close proximity, together with the roads and streams crossed
      by or near to the line.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 123. County Officers›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12303. Oath of office

content:

      and the county officer's deputies, assistants and clerks shall, before entering on
      the duties of the individual's respective offices or employments, take and subscribe
      the oath under53 Pa.C.S. § 1141(relating to form of oaths of office).

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12304. Recorded commissions (2023)
content:
Each county officer receiving a commission from the Governor shall, immediately, deliver
   the same to the recorder of deeds for recordation.  An officer may not execute any of the duties of office until the commission has
   been delivered.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 123. County Officers › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12305. Location of offices, records and papers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12305. Location of offices, records and papers (2023)
content:
(a) County seat.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (d), each county commissioner, auditor,
      controller, treasurer, sheriff, recorder of deeds, prothonotary, clerk of courts,
      clerk of orphans' court, register of wills and district attorney shall keep the individual's
      respective offices and each public record and paper of the office at the county seat
      and in buildings erected or appropriated for keeping offices and public records and
      papers.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12307. Securing from predecessors (2023)
content:
(a) Demand and receipt.--An elected or appointed person, duly commissioned to a county office, shall demand
      and receive each record, book, draft, plan, paper, seal or other official thing, including
      public money held in the office, and not provided for under Article XIII.1 of the
      act of April 9, 1929 (P.L. 343, No. 176),1known as The Fiscal Code, belonging to the office from each person who held the office
      immediately before the officer's election or appointment or from each other person
      holding or possessing the items.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 123. County Officers›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12311. Penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 123. County Officers › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12311. Penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12311. Penalty (2023)
content:
If a county officer neglects or refuses to perform a duty imposed on the officer under
   this part, any other act or by a rule of court, the officer commits, for each neglect
   or refusal, a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, shall be sentenced to pay a fine not
   exceeding $500.

      and receive each record, book, draft, plan, paper, seal or other official thing, including
      public money held in the office, and not provided for under Article XIII.1 of the
      act of April 9, 1929 (P.L. 343, No. 176),1known as The Fiscal Code, belonging to the office from each person who held the office

content:

      controller, treasurer, sheriff, recorder of deeds, prothonotary, clerk of courts,
      clerk of orphans' court, register of wills and district attorney shall keep the individual's
      respective offices and each public record and paper of the office at the county seat

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12501. Election and vacancies (2023)
content:
(a) Election.--Three county commissioners shall be elected in each county in the year 1955 and every
      fourth year thereafter.  In the election of county commissioners, each qualified elector shall vote for no
      more than two individuals.  The three individuals having the highest number of votes shall be elected.

County officers of each county may organize for themselves a State association as
   follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter C. State Associations›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12344. Other meeting expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Subchapter C. State Associations › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12344. Other meeting expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12344. Other meeting expenses (2023)
content:
(a) Equal payments.--In addition to the expenses authorized under this subchapter, the necessary expenses
      of the annual meetings under this section shall be paid in equal parts by each county
      with officers that are members of the respective associations.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter C. State Associations›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12345. Annual assessments

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12345. Annual assessments (2023)
content:
(a) County commissioners, county solicitors and chief clerks.--In addition to the expenses authorized under this subchapter, the necessary expenses
      of the association of county commissioners, county solicitors and chief clerks shall
      be apportioned among each county holding membership in the association in amounts
      provided for by the rules and regulations of each association.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12311. Penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12311. Penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12311. Penalty (2023)
content:
If a county officer neglects or refuses to perform a duty imposed on the officer under
   this part, any other act or by a rule of court, the officer commits, for each neglect
   or refusal, a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, shall be sentenced to pay a fine not
   exceeding $500.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 125. County Commissioners and Chief Clerks›Subchapter A. County Commissioners›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12505. Certified copies of proceedings

content:
Copies of the proceedings of the county commissioners and of each record in the possession
   of the county commissioners, certified by the chief clerk under the county seal, shall
   be admitted in evidence in any court of the Commonwealth.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12502. Organization (2023)
content:
The county commissioners shall meet on the first Monday of January 1956 and on the
   first Monday of January every fourth year thereafter in the office provided for the
   county commissioners at the county seat for the purpose of organization.  If the first Monday is a legal holiday, the meeting shall be held the next day.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 125. County Commissioners and Chief Clerks › Subchapter A. County Commissioners › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12503. Meetings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12503. Meetings (2023)
content:
(a) Rules.--The county commissioners shall adopt rules for the conduct and order of business and
      establish regular times and places of meetings.  A copy of the rules shall be posted in a conspicuous place in the county courthouse
      for the benefit of the public.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 125. County Commissioners and Chief Clerks›Subchapter A. County Commissioners›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12507. Expenses

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12507. Expenses (2023)
content:
A county commissioner may receive expenses necessarily incurred and actually paid
   in the discharge of the county commissioner's official duties or in the performance
   of a service, office or duty imposed upon a county commissioner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 125. County Commissioners and Chief Clerks›Subchapter A. County Commissioners›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12506. Oaths

content:
Each county commissioner may administer oaths and affirmations in each case arising
   in the performance of the duties of the office of the county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter E. Conduct of Official Business›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12360. Meetings open to public

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12360. Meetings open to public (2023)
content:
Each regular or special meeting of the county commissioners and of each board, commission
   and authority, created by or operating as an agency of a county, shall be a public
   meeting subject to 65 Pa.C.S. Ch. 7 (relating to open meetings).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 125. County Commissioners and Chief Clerks›Subchapter A. County Commissioners›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12508. Office supplies

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12508. Office supplies (2023)
content:
(a) Supplies.--The county commissioners, at the cost of the county, shall purchase and provide office
      furniture, equipment and supplies, blank books, blank dockets, books for records,
      stationery, postage, utilities, cleaning and maintenance required for each of the
      county officers whose offices are located in a county building or at another place
      at the county seat as may be designated by the county commissioners and each supply
      used by the public in connection with each office.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12509. Ordinances and resolutions (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization.--The county commissioners may adopt ordinances and resolutions prescribing the manner
      in which the powers of the county shall be carried out and generally regulating the
      affairs of the county.  The county commissioners may formulate and adopt ordinances, resolutions, rules
      and regulations pertaining to the use of property owned or used by the county and
      the conduct of individuals in, on or about the property in order to preserve the property
      and to promote and preserve public health, safety and welfare.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12501. Election and vacancies (2023)
content:
(a) Election.--Three county commissioners shall be elected in each county in the year 1955 and every
      fourth year thereafter.  In the election of county commissioners, each qualified elector shall vote for no
      more than two individuals.  The three individuals having the highest number of votes shall be elected.

      quorum for the transaction of business and, when convened after notice, shall be competent
      to perform each of the duties pertaining to the office of county commissioners.

      and file the proceedings and papers of the county commissioners, attest all orders
      and voucher checks issued by the county commissioners and perform all other duties
      pertaining to the office of chief clerk.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 127. Controller›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12706. Appointment by Governor, duties of auditors and abolition of office of auditor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 127. Controller › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12706. Appointment by Governor, duties of auditors and abolition of office of auditor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12706. Appointment by Governor, duties of auditors and abolition of office of auditor (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--If the office of controller is established in a county under section 12705 (relating
      to establishment of office of controller in counties of sixth, seventh and eighth
      classes), or by a change in class of the county not otherwise provided for by law,
      the Governor shall appoint a suitable individual to act as the controller of the county
      until a successor in office is duly elected and installed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 129. Auditors›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12901. Election and vacancies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 129. Auditors › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12901. Election and vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12901. Election and vacancies (2023)
content:
(a) Election.--In each county in which the office of controller has not been established, three county
      auditors shall be elected in 1955 and every four years thereafter.  In the election of county auditors, each qualified elector shall vote for no more
      than two individuals.  The three individuals with the highest number of votes shall be elected to the office
      of county auditor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 127. Controller›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12705. Establishment of office of controller in counties of sixth, seventh and eighth classes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 127. Controller › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12705. Establishment of office of controller in counties of sixth, seventh and eighth classes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12705. Establishment of office of controller in counties of sixth, seventh and eighth classes (2023)
content:
(a) Authorization.--The office of controller may be established in a county of the sixth, seventh and
      eighth class by the affirmative vote of a majority of the electors of the county voting
      on the question submitted, in accordance with this section, at the general election
      when the auditor of the county is in the third year of the auditor's term.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 127. Controller›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12701. Election, term and seal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 127. Controller › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12701. Election, term and seal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12701. Election, term and seal (2023)
content:
(a) Election of controller.--At the municipal election immediately preceding the expiration of the term of the
      controller in office on January 1, 1956, and every four years thereafter, the qualified
      electors of each county of the third, fourth and fifth class and every other county
      in which the office of controller has been or may be established, including counties
      in which the office was established by general law or otherwise when the counties
      were in a higher classification, shall elect one resident of the county to serve as
      controller for the term of four years beginning the first Monday of January after
      the controller's election or until a successor is qualified to serve in office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 127. Controller›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12702. Eligibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 127. Controller › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12702. Eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12702. Eligibility (2023)
content:
(a) Office holders.--An individual holding office under the United States shall not be eligible to the
      office of county controller while in office and for one year after leaving office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 129. Auditors›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12903. Meetings and quorum
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 129. Auditors › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12903. Meetings and quorum
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12903. Meetings and quorum (2023)
content:
(a) Meetings.--The auditors shall meet at the county seat on the first Monday of January in each
      year for the purpose of organizing and to begin the audit of the fiscal affairs of
      the county for the immediately preceding fiscal year.  If the first Monday in January is a legal holiday, the meeting shall be held the
      first day after the first Monday in January.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 127. Controller›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12707. Expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 127. Controller › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12707. Expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12707. Expenses (2023)
content:
The county controller and the county controller's deputy, clerks and auditors shall
   be allowed their expenses necessarily incurred and actually paid in the discharge
   of their official duties or in the performance of any service or duty imposed.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 131. Treasurer › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13101. County treasurer and eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13101. County treasurer and eligibility (2023)
content:
No judge, clerk or prothonotary of any court, register of wills, recorder of deeds,
   county commissioner or county controller shall be eligible to serve as county treasurer
   during their continuance in office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 129. Auditors›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12902. Eligibility
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 129. Auditors › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12902. Eligibility
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 12902. Eligibility (2023)
content:
(a) Treasurers.--An individual may not be eligible to the office of county auditor if the individual
      has been the treasurer of the county within the previous two years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 131. Treasurer›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13106. Deputy treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 131. Treasurer › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13106. Deputy treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13106. Deputy treasurer (2023)
content:
The county treasurer may appoint a deputy county treasurer who shall perform duties
   as prescribed by the county treasurer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 131. Treasurer›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13106.1. Second deputy treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 131. Treasurer › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13106.1. Second deputy treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13106.1. Second deputy treasurer (2023)
content:
The county treasurer may appoint a second deputy treasurer.  The second deputy treasurer shall possess and discharge all the rights, powers and
   duties of the principal deputy treasurer during the principal deputy treasurer's and
   treasurer's temporary absence.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13303. Employees in certain counties (2023)
content:
In counties of the second class A and third class, the county solicitor may, with
   the consent of the county commissioners, employ clerks or assistants as may be necessary
   in the discharge of the county solicitor's duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 131. Treasurer›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13105. Misapplication of money collected for specific purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 131. Treasurer › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13105. Misapplication of money collected for specific purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13105. Misapplication of money collected for specific purposes (2023)
content:
If money is collected by law in a county and is in the possession or control of the
   treasurer of the county, it shall be unlawful for the treasurer to apply the money
   to any other purpose than that for which the money was collected unless otherwise
   authorized by law.  A misapplication of money under this section shall constitute a violation of18 Pa.C.S. § 3927(relating to theft by failure to make required disposition of funds received).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 133. County Solicitor›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13301. Appointment and qualifications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 133. County Solicitor › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13301. Appointment and qualifications
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13301. Appointment and qualifications (2023)
content:
The county commissioners shall appoint a county solicitor.  The county solicitor shall be an attorney at law admitted to practice in the courts
   of this Commonwealth and may be an individual, a law firm, a partnership, an association
   or a professional corporation.  Before entering upon the duties of office, the county solicitor shall file with
   the county commissioners an agreement to pay all fees, attorney fees and commissions
   received from every source as county solicitor into the county treasury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 135. Engineer›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13501. County engineer, appointment and term
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 135. Engineer › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13501. County engineer, appointment and term
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13501. County engineer, appointment and term (2023)
content:
The county commissioners may appoint a professional engineer in civil engineering
   or an engineering firm as the county engineer.  The engineer shall serve at the pleasure of the county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13703. Chief deputy and petition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13703. Chief deputy and petition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13703. Chief deputy and petition (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--The sheriff of each county shall appoint, by commission duly recorded in the office
      for recording deeds, a chief deputy.  The chief deputy's appointment shall be revocable by the sheriff by a signed revocation
      recorded in the office for recording deeds.  The chief deputy, during continuance in office, may perform any duty incumbent upon
      the sheriff, which shall have the effect in law as if the duty had been done by the
      sheriff in person, regardless of the ability or temporary disability of the sheriff
      to act, while the sheriff continues in office.  Nothing in this subsection shall be construed to relieve the sheriff or the sheriff's
      sureties from liability upon the official bond of the sheriff or the sheriff's sureties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 133. County Solicitor›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13304. Assistant county solicitors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 133. County Solicitor › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13304. Assistant county solicitors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13304. Assistant county solicitors (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--Except as provided under subsection (b), the county commissioners may appoint one
      or more assistant county solicitors or special counsel.  The assistant county solicitors or special counsel shall be attorneys at law admitted
      to practice in the courts of this Commonwealth.  The assistant county solicitors and special counsel shall perform duties in connection
      with the legal affairs of the county as may be assigned by the county commissioners
      or the county solicitor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13701. Unfinished business of outgoing sheriff
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13701. Unfinished business of outgoing sheriff
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13701. Unfinished business of outgoing sheriff (2023)
content:
(a) Unfinished business.--An outgoing sheriff shall deliver all unfinished and unexecuted writs and process
      to the sheriff's successor.  The sheriff's successor shall receive and execute the writs and process as if the
      writs and process had been originally issued and directed to the sheriff's successor
      and carry out and complete all other official duties of the outgoing sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13706. Deputy sheriff's qualifications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13706. Deputy sheriff's qualifications

content:
(a) Requirements.--A sheriff may not appoint an individual as a chief deputy or any other deputy sheriff
      unless the sheriff files with the prothonotary, before the appointment of the individual,
      the name and photograph of the individual and an affidavit of the individual setting
      forth the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13705. Deputies and clerks
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13705. Deputies and clerks
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13705. Deputies and clerks (2023)
content:
The sheriff of each county may appoint deputies and clerks to positions established
   in accordance with section 14723 (relating to number and compensation of officers,
   deputies, assistants, clerks and employees and revisions of salary schedules) for
   the transaction of the business of the sheriff's office.  The sheriff may revoke the appointment of deputies in the same manner as the chief
   deputy.  In counties of the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth class, the sheriff
   may also appoint as necessary special deputies to assist the sheriff in executing
   a civil or criminal process or court order or in preserving the peace when an emergency
   arises.  A special deputy shall serve for a period only as necessary to conduct the special
   deputy's duties under this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13702. Deputy action authorized
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13702. Deputy action authorized
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13702. Deputy action authorized (2023)
content:
If the sheriff is required by law to act in person under or by virtue of any writ
   or process issued by a court of the Commonwealth, the sheriff may act either in person
   or by a regularly appointed deputy sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13708. Filed items and public records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13708. Filed items and public records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13708. Filed items and public records (2023)
content:
The name, photograph and affidavit filed under section 13706 (relating to deputy sheriff's
   qualifications) with the prothonotary shall constitute a public record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13709. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13709. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13709. Public list of applicants for deputy sheriff (2023)
content:
The sheriff shall, from time to time, prepare a list of the names of all the individuals
   who have applied for appointment as deputy sheriff and meet the qualifications for
   the position.  The list shall be posted in a public place for a period of not less than 10 days.  After the 10 days have elapsed, the list shall be filed in the office of the prothonotary.  No deputy sheriffs shall be appointed by the sheriff whose names do not appear on
   the list.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13711. Penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13711. Penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13711. Penalties (2023)
content:
A sheriff, deputy sheriff or other county police officer or another official of the
   county or an individual, association or corporation that violates the provisions of
   section 13706 (relating to deputy sheriff's qualifications), 13709 (relating to public
   list of applicants for deputy sheriff) or 13710 (relating to private services, gifts
   and payments prohibited) commits a misdemeanor and shall, upon conviction, be sentenced
   to pay a fine of not less than $100 nor more than $500 or to undergo imprisonment
   for not less than 90 days nor more than two years, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13712. Construction

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13704. Real estate deputies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13704. Real estate deputies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13704. Real estate deputies (2023)
content:
The sheriff may appoint a real estate deputy to administer all matters relating to
   the sheriff's sales of real estate and distributions of the proceeds of the sheriff's
   sales of real estate.  The real estate deputy's appointment shall be made and be revocable as provided
   for the chief deputy.  The real estate deputy may perform all duties incumbent upon the sheriff in the
   same manner as the chief deputy and the same effect in law as if the official duties
   had been performed by the sheriff in person.  The duties shall include the execution and acknowledgment of sheriff's deeds for
   real estate upon receipt of the purchase price for the real estate.  Nothing in this section shall operate to relieve the sheriff or the sheriff's sureties
   from liability upon official bond of the sheriff or the sheriff's sureties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13707. False statements in deputy's affidavit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13707. False statements in deputy's affidavit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13707. False statements in deputy's affidavit (2023)
content:
Any false statement contained in an affidavit filed under section 13706 (relating
   to deputy sheriff's qualifications) shall constitute and shall be punishable as perjury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13713. Chief deputy sheriff to act as sheriff in case of vacancy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13713. Chief deputy sheriff to act as sheriff in case of vacancy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13713. Chief deputy sheriff to act as sheriff in case of vacancy (2023)
content:
If a sheriff is legally removed from office or dies or resigns before the expiration
   of the term for which the sheriff was commissioned, the chief deputy sheriff shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13912. Duties regarding county morgues
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13912. Duties regarding county morgues
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13912. Duties regarding county morgues (2023)
content:
(a) Coroner.--The coroner of a county in which a county morgue is established shall have the following
      duties:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13714. Sheriff to keep docket
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13714. Sheriff to keep docket
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13714. Sheriff to keep docket (2023)
content:
A sheriff shall provide and keep in the office of sheriff a book in which the sheriff
   shall enter all writs that may be received and the proceedings of all the writs.  At the expiration of the term of office, the book shall be deposited in the office
   of the prothonotary for the inspection of all interested members of the public.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13902. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13902. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13902. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13901. Applicability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13901. Applicability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13901. Applicability (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise expressly provided under this chapter, this chapter shall apply
   to counties of the second class, second class A and third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh
   and eighth class.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13913. Removal of bodies to morgue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13913. Removal of bodies to morgue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13913. Removal of bodies to morgue (2023)
content:
(a) Unidentified or unclaimed body.--If the body of a deceased individual is unidentified or unclaimed by a proper individual
      located within the county, the body shall be removed to the county morgue or, in a
      county of the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth class, to a facility
      serving in lieu of the county morgue.  If necessary, the coroner shall have the body properly embalmed or prepared for
      preservation for the length of time the coroner determines is required to determine
      the deceased's identity, the identity of a party responsible for the deceased and
      the cause and manner of death.  The body may only be examined or inspected by an individual authorized by the coroner
      or who is admitted in the coroner's presence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13715. Not to exercise office until commission granted and recorded and penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13715. Not to exercise office until commission granted and recorded and penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13715. Not to exercise office until commission granted and recorded and penalty (2023)
content:
An individual elected or appointed to the office of sheriff may not execute any of
   the duties of office before a commission is duly granted to the sheriff by the Governor
   and properly recorded, under a penalty of imprisonment for a term not exceeding six
   months, at the discretion of the court of common pleas.  The individual elected or appointed to the office of sheriff shall be liable to
   a person injured by acts done by the sheriff under the purview of the office of sheriff.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 137. Sheriff›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13710. Private services, gifts and payments prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 137. Sheriff › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13710. Private services, gifts and payments prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13710. Private services, gifts and payments prohibited (2023)
content: (a) Services, gifts and payments.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13917. Requests for examinations and reports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13917. Requests for examinations and reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13917. Requests for examinations and reports (2023)
content:
(a) Requests.--A request for an examination or other professional service by another county or person
      may be complied with at the discretion of the coroner under guidelines established
      by the county commissioners.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13911. Deputies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13911. Deputies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13911. Deputies (2023)
content:
The coroner may appoint a deputy to act in the coroner's place and may appoint staff
   to positions established in accordance with section 14723 (relating to number and
   compensation of officers, deputies, assistants, clerks and employees and revisions
   of salary schedules) as the coroner determines.  A deputy shall have the same powers as the coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13914. Removal of body, burial and vehicle
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13914. Removal of body, burial and vehicle
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13914. Removal of body, burial and vehicle (2023)
content:
(a) Removal and burial.--The county commissioners shall, in consultation with the coroner, provide for the
      removal of a body of a deceased individual to and from the morgue and for the burial
      of an unclaimed body.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13915. Unclaimed property and sales
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13915. Unclaimed property and sales
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13915. Unclaimed property and sales (2023)
content: (a) Duties.--The coroner shall safely keep all of the following in the coroner's charge:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13920. Child deaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13920. Child deaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13920. Child deaths (2023)
content:
(a) Duties.--A coroner shall perform or order an autopsy to be conducted for the sudden unexplained
      death of a child who is not more than three years of age.  If an autopsy is required, the autopsy shall be conducted in the manner the coroner
      determines is the least invasive manner appropriate.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13919. Autopsy, inquest and records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13919. Autopsy, inquest and records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13919. Autopsy, inquest and records (2023)
content:
(a) Autopsy.--If, after investigation, the coroner is unable to determine the cause and manner of
      death, the coroner shall perform or order an autopsy on the body.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13921. Sudden death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13921. Sudden death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13921. Sudden death (2023)
content: (a) Recognition.--The coroner shall recognize a death as sudden if all of the following apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13916. Private morgue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13916. Private morgue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13916. Private morgue (2023)
content:
In a county of the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth class in which
   a county morgue is not maintained, the coroner may have a body that the coroner may
   admit to a county morgue removed to a private facility.  The county commissioners shall procure by contract, as under Chapter 151 (relating
   to contracts), the use of a private facility in consultation with the coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13926. Certificate of cause of death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13926. Certificate of cause of death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13926. Certificate of cause of death (2023)
content: A coroner shall issue a certificate of cause of death in each case:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13925. Cooperation with other counties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13925. Cooperation with other counties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13925. Cooperation with other counties (2023)
content:
If one or more coroners deem it necessary to establish a facility for conducting forensic
   testing and autopsies, a county may establish and operate the facility.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13918. Coroner's investigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13918. Coroner's investigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13918. Coroner's investigation (2023)
content:
(a) Duties.--The coroner having a view of the body shall investigate the facts and circumstances
      concerning a death that appears to have happened within the county, notwithstanding
      where the cause of the death may have occurred, for the purpose of determining if
      an autopsy or inquest should be conducted in the following cases:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13923. Release of coroner's jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13923. Release of coroner's jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13923. Release of coroner's jurisdiction (2023)
content:
If a coroner assumes jurisdiction of a body under the provisions of this chapter or
   any other law, the body may not be released or removed from the coroner's jurisdiction
   except upon the coroner's directions and consent in accordance with law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13928. Jury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13928. Jury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13928. Jury (2023)
content:
(a) Jury.--The coroner may summon a jury of six individuals and two alternates to be selected
      from the jury panels of the court of common pleas.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13927. Subpoena and attachment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13927. Subpoena and attachment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13927. Subpoena and attachment (2023)
content:
The coroner may issue a subpoena and attachment, which shall be served and executed
   by the sheriff, coroner or coroner's deputy, for the following purposes:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13929. Oaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13929. Oaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13929. Oaths (2023)
content:
The coroner may administer an oath and affirmation to an individual brought or appearing
   before the coroner.  An individual who falsely swears or affirms during the examination commits perjury.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13924. Cooperation with district attorney
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13924. Cooperation with district attorney
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13924. Cooperation with district attorney (2023)
content:
In the exercise of duties under this chapter, the coroner shall consult with and advise
   the district attorney as may be practicable.  The district attorney may act as counsel to the coroner in matters relating to inquests.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13932. Vacancy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13932. Vacancy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13932. Vacancy (2023)
content:
(a) Removal, death or resignation.--If a coroner is legally removed from office, dies or resigns before the expiration
      of the term for which the coroner was elected or appointed, the chief deputy coroner
      shall execute the office of coroner, perform related duties and receive and retain
      the compensation provided by law for the coroner until another coroner is appointed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13930. Commitment to county prison
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13930. Commitment to county prison
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13930. Commitment to county prison (2023)

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13922. Prohibition on moving a body
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13922. Prohibition on moving a body
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13922. Prohibition on moving a body (2023)
content:
(a) Moving a body.--Except as provided under subsection (b), if a coroner has jurisdiction to investigate
      the facts and circumstances of death, the body and the surroundings of the body shall
      be left untouched until either of the following occurs:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13931. Excluded individuals

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13931. Excluded individuals (2023)
content: The following apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13902. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13902. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13902. Definitions (2023)
content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter C. Fees and Cost Recovery›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13951. Disposition costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter C. Fees and Cost Recovery › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13951. Disposition costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13951. Disposition costs (2023)
content:
(a) Cost of disposition.--If a legal representative makes a claim to property after disposition of the deceased
      has occurred at county expense, any property retained from the deceased by the coroner
      in accordance with section 13915 (relating to unclaimed property and sales) shall
      be subject to sale to cover the cost of disposition with the balance, if any, going
      to the legal representatives.  No property shall be sold under this subsection unless the coroner has provided
      written notice to the representative of all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13933. Anatomical gifts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13933. Anatomical gifts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13933. Anatomical gifts (2023)
content:
The coroner may order the removal of parts of a decedent's body for donation purposes
   in accordance with 20 Pa.C.S. Ch. 86 (relating to anatomical gifts).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13935. Records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13935. Records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13935. Records (2023)
content:
In counties of the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth classes, every
   coroner, within 30 days after the end of each year, shall deposit all official records
   and papers for the preceding year in the office of the prothonotary for the inspection
   of interested members of the public.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13934. Execution of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13934. Execution of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13934. Execution of office (2023)
content:
An individual elected or appointed to the office of coroner may not execute any of
   the duties of the office before a commission has been issued to the coroner by the
   Governor and properly recorded.  An individual who violates this section may be sentenced to imprisonment for a term
   of not more than six months.  The individual shall be liable to a person injured by an act done by the individual
   under authority of the office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13911. Deputies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13911. Deputies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13911. Deputies (2023)
content:
The coroner may appoint a deputy to act in the coroner's place and may appoint staff
   to positions established in accordance with section 14723 (relating to number and
   compensation of officers, deputies, assistants, clerks and employees and revisions
   of salary schedules) as the coroner determines.  A deputy shall have the same powers as the coroner.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13901. Applicability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Subchapter A. Preliminary Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13901. Applicability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13901. Applicability (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise expressly provided under this chapter, this chapter shall apply
   to counties of the second class, second class A and third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh
   and eighth class.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Chapter 139. Coroner›Subchapter C. Fees and Cost Recovery›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13952. Fees for reports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Chapter 139. Coroner › Subchapter C. Fees and Cost Recovery › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13952. Fees for reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13952. Fees for reports (2023)
content:
The coroner shall charge and collect a fee of $500 for an autopsy report, $100 for
   a toxicology report, $100 for an inquisition or coroner's report, $50 for a cremation
   or disposition authorization and other fees as may be established for other reports
   or documents requested by nongovernmental agencies in order to investigate a claim
   asserted under a policy of insurance or to determine liability for the death of the
   deceased.  The fees collected under this section shall be accounted for and paid to the county
   treasurer in accordance with section 14960 (relating to receipts and accounts of money
   due county) and shall be used to defray the expenses involved in the county complying
   with the training of coroners or coroner office personnel, as may be required or authorized
   under this part or any other act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13913. Removal of bodies to morgue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties › Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class › Subchapter B. General Provisions › PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13913. Removal of bodies to morgue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13913. Removal of bodies to morgue (2023)
content:
(a) Unidentified or unclaimed body.--If the body of a deceased individual is unidentified or unclaimed by a proper individual
      located within the county, the body shall be removed to the county morgue or, in a
      county of the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth class, to a facility
      serving in lieu of the county morgue.  If necessary, the coroner shall have the body properly embalmed or prepared for
      preservation for the length of time the coroner determines is required to determine
      the deceased's identity, the identity of a party responsible for the deceased and
      the cause and manner of death.  The body may only be examined or inspected by an individual authorized by the coroner
      or who is admitted in the coroner's presence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 16 Pa.C.S.A. Counties›Part IV. Counties of the Second Class A through Eighth Class›Subchapter B. General Provisions›PA ST 16 Pa.C.S.A. § 13912. Duties regarding county morgues

content:
