path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 7. Members, Directors and Officers›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 715. Actions by members to enforce a secondary right
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 7. Members, Directors and Officers › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 715. Actions by members to enforce a secondary right
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 715. Actions by members to enforce a secondary right (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In any action brought to enforce a secondary right on the part of one or more members
      against any officer or director or former officer or director of a credit union because
      the corporation refuses to enforce rights which may properly be asserted by it, the
      plaintiff or plaintiffs must aver and it must be made to appear that the plaintiff
      or each plaintiff was a member of the corporation at the time of the transaction of
      which he complains or that his membership devolved upon him by operation of law from
      a person who was a member at that time.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 7. Members, Directors and Officers›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Executive committee
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 7. Members, Directors and Officers › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Executive committee
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 710. Executive committee (2023)
content:
The directors may appoint from their own number an executive committee of not less
   than three directors, who may be authorized to act for the board in all respects,
   subject to such conditions and limitations as prescribed by the board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 7. Members, Directors and Officers›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Loan procedures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 7. Members, Directors and Officers › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Loan procedures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 713. Loan procedures (2023)
content:
(a) Credit committee.--If the bylaws provide for a credit committee, the credit committee shall have the
      supervision of all loans to members other than first mortgage loans, except to the
      extent approval of such mortgage loans has been delegated to the credit committee,
      and loans to other credit unions and Federal credit unions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 9. Amendment of Articles›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Articles of amendment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 9. Amendment of Articles › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Articles of amendment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 902. Articles of amendment (2023)
content:
The articles of amendment shall be signed by an officer of the credit union and shall
   set forth:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 11. Conversion, Merger and Consolidation›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Conversion from Federal credit union
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 11. Conversion, Merger and Consolidation › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Conversion from Federal credit union
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Conversion from Federal credit union (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A Federal credit union may be converted into a credit union subject to the provisions

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 9. Amendment of Articles›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Filing and review of articles of amendment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 9. Amendment of Articles › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Filing and review of articles of amendment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 903. Filing and review of articles of amendment (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Articles of amendment shall be filed with the department.  If the department finds that the articles of amendment conform to law, it shall
      endorse its approval thereon and forward the articles of amendment to the Department
      of State.  Upon receipt of the articles of amendment, the Department of State shall file the
      same.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 9. Amendment of Articles›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Place of business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 9. Amendment of Articles › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Place of business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 904. Place of business (2023)
content:
(a) Change in principal place of business.--A credit union may change its place of business upon the filing of a statement of
      change of principal place of business with the Department of State and the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 11. Conversion, Merger and Consolidation›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Adoption of plan
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 11. Conversion, Merger and Consolidation › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Adoption of plan
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1104. Adoption of plan (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The board of directors of each of the credit unions, Federal credit unions or out-of-State
      credit unions which desire to merge or consolidate shall, by resolution adopted by
      at least a majority of all the members of each board, approve a plan of merger or
      consolidation setting forth the terms and conditions of the merger or consolidation
      and the mode of carrying the same into effect, the manner and basis of converting
      the shares of each credit union, Federal credit union or out-of-State credit union
      into shares or other securities or obligations of the surviving or new credit union,
      Federal credit union or out-of-State credit union, and such other details and provisions
      as are deemed necessary.  Except where the approval of the members is not required, the board of directors
      shall direct that the plan be submitted to a vote of the members of such credit union,
      Federal credit union or out-of-State credit union entitled to vote thereon at an annual
      or special meeting of the members to be held on not less than 15 days prior notice
      thereof given to each member of record, which notice shall state the place, day, hour
      and purpose of the meeting and shall have included therein or enclosed therewith a
      copy or summary of the plan of merger or consolidation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 13. Dissolution›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1301. Dissolution authorized
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 13. Dissolution › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1301. Dissolution authorized
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1301. Dissolution authorized (2023)
content:
Any credit union may elect to dissolve voluntarily and wind up its affairs in the
   manner provided in this chapter.  However, if it shall appear to the department, upon an examination of the business,
   assets and affairs of the credit union, that its assets will probably be insufficient
   to pay in full its members and creditors, it shall take possession of the business
   and property of the credit union and retain possession until its affairs are finally
   liquidated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions›Chapter 11. Conversion, Merger and Consolidation›PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Merger and consolidation authorized
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 17 Pa.C.S.A. Credit Unions › Chapter 11. Conversion, Merger and Consolidation › PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Merger and consolidation authorized
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 17 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Merger and consolidation authorized (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A credit union subject to this title may merge or consolidate with other credit unions,
      with Federal credit unions, with out-of-State credit unions or with a combination
      of other credit unions, Federal credit unions and out-of-State credit unions to form

      any of its powers or opened for business with its proposed members within one year
      after the date of its incorporation or such longer time as the department may allow,

      the applicable facts and stating that articles of incorporation have been forfeited

content:

      credit union in this Commonwealth with the approval of the department as long as a
      credit union chartered under the laws of this Commonwealth is permitted to do business
      in the state in which the credit union is organized.

content:
(a) General rule.--A person is not guilty of an offense unless his liability is based on conduct which
      includes a voluntary act or the omission to perform an act of which he is physically
      capable.

content:
(a) Minimum requirements of culpability.--Except as provided in section 305 of this title (relating to limitations on scope
      of culpability requirements), a person is not guilty of an offense unless he acted
      intentionally, knowingly, recklessly or negligently, as the law may require, with
      respect to each material element of the offense.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 105. Principles of construction (2023)
content:
The provisions of this title shall be construed according to the fair import of their
   terms but when the language is susceptible of differing constructions it shall be
   interpreted to further the general purposes stated in this title and the special purposes
   of the particular provision involved.  The discretionary powers conferred by this title shall be exercised in accordance
   with the criteria stated in this title and, in so far as such criteria are not decisive,
   to further the general purposes stated in this title.

content:

      to limitation of time).

content:

      to offenses defined by this title or by any other statute.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 1. General Provisions›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 1. General Provisions › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 101. Short title of title

content: This title shall be known and may be cited as the “Crimes Code.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 5. General Principles of Justification›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Justification a defense
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 5. General Principles of Justification › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Justification a defense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 502. Justification a defense (2023)
content:
In any prosecution based on conduct which is justifiable under this chapter, justification
   is a defense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Culpability›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 315. Insanity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Culpability › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 315. Insanity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 315. Insanity (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The mental soundness of an actor engaged in conduct charged to constitute an offense
      shall only be a defense to the charged offense when the actor proves by a preponderance
      of evidence that the actor was legally insane at the time of the commission of the
      offense.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Culpability›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Liability for conduct of another; complicity
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Culpability › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Liability for conduct of another; complicity
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 306. Liability for conduct of another; complicity (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person is guilty of an offense if it is committed by his own conduct or by the conduct
      of another person for which he is legally accountable, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Culpability›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 314. Guilty but mentally ill
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Culpability › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 314. Guilty but mentally ill
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 314. Guilty but mentally ill (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person who timely offers a defense of insanity in accordance with the Rules of Criminal
      Procedure may be found “guilty but mentally ill” at trial if the trier of facts finds,
      beyond a reasonable doubt, that the person is guilty of an offense, was mentally ill
      at the time of the commission of the offense and was not legally insane at the time
      of the commission of the offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Culpability›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 311. Consent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Culpability › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 311. Consent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 311. Consent (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The consent of the victim to conduct charged to constitute an offense or to the result
      thereof is a defense if such consent negatives an element of the offense or precludes
      the infliction of the harm or evil sought to be prevented by the law defining the
      offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 3. Culpability›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Duress
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Culpability › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Duress
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 309. Duress (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--It is a defense that the actor engaged in the conduct charged to constitute an offense
      because he was coerced to do so by the use of, or a threat to use, unlawful force
      against his person or the person of another, which a person of reasonable firmness
      in his situation would have been unable to resist.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 3. Culpability › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 308. Intoxication or drugged condition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 308. Intoxication or drugged condition (2023)
content:
Neither voluntary intoxication nor voluntary drugged condition is a defense to a criminal
   charge, nor may evidence of such conditions be introduced to negative the element
   of intent of the offense, except that evidence of such intoxication or drugged condition
   of the defendant may be offered by the defendant whenever it is relevant to reduce
   murder from a higher degree to a lower degree of murder.

content:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 906. Multiple convictions of inchoate crimes barred (2023)
content:

   attempt, criminal solicitation or criminal conspiracy for conduct designed to commit
   or to culminate in the commission of the same crime.

      any act which constitutes a substantial step toward the commission of that crime.

      and Cosmetic Act1involving the manufacture of a controlled substance, the court shall order the person

      equipment and supplies, of any clandestine laboratory used by the person to manufacture

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part I. Preliminary Provisions›Chapter 11. Authorized Disposition of Offenders›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 1108. District attorneys' standing and interest in prisoner litigation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part I. Preliminary Provisions › Chapter 11. Authorized Disposition of Offenders › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 1108. District attorneys' standing and interest in prisoner litigation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 1108. District attorneys' standing and interest in prisoner litigation (2023)
content:
The district attorney shall receive written notice of, and shall have automatic standing
   and a legal interest in, any proceeding which may involve the release or nonadmission
   of county prisoners, delinquents or detainees due to the fact, duration or other conditions
   of custody.  In addition to the district attorney's rights in such a proceeding, the district
   attorney may seek any equitable relief necessary to protect the district attorney's
   interest in the continued institutional custody and admission of county prisoners,
   delinquents or detainees.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Insults to national or Commonwealth flag (2023)
content:
A person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the second degree if he maliciously takes down,
   defiles, injures, removes or in any manner damages, insults, or destroys any American
   flag or the flag of the Commonwealth which is displayed anywhere.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Display of flag at public meetings (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person is guilty of a summary offense if, being directly or indirectly in charge
      of any public gathering, in any place, he fails at such gathering to display publicly
      and visibly the flag of the United States reasonably clean and in good repair.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Drug delivery resulting in death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Drug delivery resulting in death (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person commits a felony of the first degree if the person intentionally administers,
      dispenses, delivers, gives, prescribes, sells or distributes any controlled substance
      or counterfeit controlled substance in violation of section 13(a)(14) or (30) of the
      act of April 14, 1972 (P.L. 233, No. 64),1known as The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act, and another person
      dies as a result of using the substance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Criminal homicide

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Criminal homicide (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person is guilty of criminal homicide if he intentionally, knowingly, recklessly
      or negligently causes the death of another human being.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Murder

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Murder (2023)
content:
(a) Murder of the first degree.--A criminal homicide constitutes murder of the first degree when it is committed by
      an intentional killing.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 26. Crimes Against Unborn Child › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2603. Criminal homicide of unborn child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2603. Criminal homicide of unborn child (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--An individual commits criminal homicide of an unborn child if the individual intentionally,
      knowingly, recklessly or negligently causes the death of an unborn child in violation
      of section 2604 (relating to murder of unborn child) or 2605 (relating to voluntary
      manslaughter of unborn child).

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Causing or aiding suicide (2023)
content:
(a) Causing suicide as criminal homicide.--A person may be convicted of criminal homicide for causing another to die by suicide
      only if he intentionally causes such suicide by force, duress or deception.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504. Involuntary manslaughter (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person is guilty of involuntary manslaughter when as a direct result of the doing
      of an unlawful act in a reckless or grossly negligent manner, or the doing of a lawful
      act in a reckless or grossly negligent manner, he causes the death of another person.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Criminal homicide of law enforcement officer

content:
(a) Murder of a law enforcement officer of the first degree.--A person commits murder of a law enforcement officer of the first degree who intentionally
      kills a law enforcement officer while in the performance of duty knowing the victim
      is a law enforcement officer.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2606. Aggravated assault of unborn child (2023)
content:
(a) Offense.--A person commits aggravated assault of an unborn child if he attempts to cause serious
      bodily injury to the unborn child or causes such injury intentionally, knowingly or
      recklessly under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to the life of the
      unborn child.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 27. Assault › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2703.1. Aggravated harassment by prisoner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2703.1. Aggravated harassment by prisoner (2023)
content:
A person who is confined in or committed to any local or county detention facility,
   jail or prison or any State penal or correctional institution or other State penal
   or correctional facility located in this Commonwealth commits a felony of the third
   degree if he, while so confined or committed or while undergoing transportation to
   or from such an institution or facility in or to which he was confined or committed,
   intentionally or knowingly causes or attempts to cause another to come into contact
   with blood, seminal fluid, saliva, urine or feces by throwing, tossing, spitting or
   expelling such fluid or material.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2710. Ethnic intimidation (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person commits the offense of ethnic intimidation if, with malicious intention toward
      the race, color, religion or national origin of another individual or group of individuals,
      he commits an offense under any other provision of this article or under Chapter 33
      (relating to arson, criminal mischief and other property destruction) exclusive of
      section 3307 (relating to institutional vandalism) or under section 3503 (relating
      to criminal trespass) with respect to such individual or his or her property or with
      respect to one or more members of such group or to their property.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 27. Assault › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2711. Probable cause arrests in domestic violence cases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2711. Probable cause arrests in domestic violence cases (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A police officer shall have the same right of arrest without a warrant as in a felony
      whenever he has probable cause to believe the defendant has violated section 2504
      (relating to involuntary manslaughter), 2701 (relating to simple assault), 2702(a)(3),
      (4) and (5) (relating to aggravated assault), 2705 (relating to recklessly endangering
      another person), 2706 (relating to terroristic threats), 2709.1 (relating to stalking)
      or 2718 (relating to strangulation) against a family or household member although
      the offense did not take place in the presence of the police officer.  A police officer may not arrest a person pursuant to this section without first
      observing recent physical injury to the victim or other corroborative evidence.  For the purposes of this subsection, the term “family or household member” has the meaning given that term in23 Pa.C.S. § 6102(relating to definitions).

content:

      is a sports official who was assaulted during a sports event or was assaulted as a
      result of his or her official acts as a sports official, is guilty of assault on a
      sports official.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2714. Unauthorized administration of intoxicant (2023)
content:

   under section 3121(a)(4) (relating to rape), 3123(a)(4) (relating to involuntary deviate
   sexual intercourse), 3125(5) (relating to aggravated indecent assault) or 3126(a)(5)
   (relating to indecent assault), he or she substantially impairs the complainant's
   power to appraise or control his or her conduct by administering, without the knowledge
   of the complainant, drugs or other intoxicants.

content:

   or 2804 (relating to organizational hazing) the court may, in addition to any other
   sentence authorized under law, direct the defendant to forfeit property which was
   involved in the violation for which the defendant was convicted.  The forfeiture shall be conducted in accordance with42 Pa.C.S. §§ 5803(relating to asset forfeiture), 5805 (relating to forfeiture procedure), 5806 (relating
   to motion for return of property), 5807 (relating to restrictions on use), 5807.1
   (relating to prohibition on adoptive seizures) and 5808 (relating to exceptions).

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 29. Kidnapping › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2903. False imprisonment

content:
(a) Offense defined.--Except as provided under subsection (b) or (c), a person commits a misdemeanor of
      the second degree if he knowingly restrains another unlawfully so as to interfere
      substantially with his liberty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 29. Kidnapping›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2910. Luring a child into a motor vehicle or structure
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 29. Kidnapping › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2910. Luring a child into a motor vehicle or structure
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2910. Luring a child into a motor vehicle or structure (2023)
content:
(a) Offense.--Unless the circumstances reasonably indicate that the child is in need of assistance,
      a person who lures or attempts to lure a child into a motor vehicle or structure without
      the consent, express or implied, of the child's parent or guardian commits an offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 29. Kidnapping›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2907. Disposition of ransom
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 29. Kidnapping › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2907. Disposition of ransom
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2907. Disposition of ransom (2023)
content:
A person, other than a member of the family or an intermediary of the family of a
   person held for ransom, who knowingly receives, retains or disposes of any money or
   other property of another knowing that the money or other property constitutes a ransom
   derived from an offense under this chapter, or has reason to believe that such money
   or other property is ransom derived from an offense under this chapter, is guilty
   of a felony of the third degree.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 29. Kidnapping › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2905. Interference with custody of committed persons
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2905. Interference with custody of committed persons (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person is guilty of a misdemeanor of the second degree if he knowingly or recklessly
      takes or entices any committed person away from lawful custody when he is not privileged
      to do so.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3016. Obstruction of justice (2023)
content:
A person who commits a violation of Subchapter B of Chapter 49 (relating to victim
   and witness intimidation)1or Chapter 51 (relating to obstructing governmental operations) that in any way interferes
   with or prevents the enforcement of this chapter shall be subject to the same penalties
   that may be imposed for the offense for which the person has been charged under this
   chapter.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 30. Human Trafficking›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3012. Involuntary servitude
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 30. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3012. Involuntary servitude (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person commits a felony of the first degree if the person knowingly, through any
      of the means described in subsection (b), subjects an individual to labor servitude
      or sexual servitude, except where the conduct is permissible under Federal or State
      law other than this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 29. Kidnapping›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2909. Concealment of whereabouts of a child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 29. Kidnapping › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2909. Concealment of whereabouts of a child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2909. Concealment of whereabouts of a child (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person who removes a child from the child's known place of residence with the intent
      to conceal the child's whereabouts from the child's parent or guardian, unless concealment
      is authorized by court order or is a reasonable response to domestic violence or child
      abuse, commits a felony of the third degree.  For purposes of this subsection, the term “removes” includes personally removing the child from the child's known place of residence,
      causing the child to be removed from the child's known place of residence, preventing
      the child from returning or being returned to the child's known place of residence
      and, when the child's parent or guardian has a reasonable expectation that the person
      will return the child, failing to return the child to the child's known place of residence.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3018. Evidence and defenses to human trafficking (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Evidence of the age of the victim of human trafficking with respect to the age of
      consent to sex or legal age of marriage shall not constitute a defense in a prosecution
      for a violation under this chapter, nor shall the evidence preclude a finding of a
      violation under this chapter.

      trafficking, willfully or with intent to defraud, fails or refuses to pay wages for
      or otherwise causes financial harm to an individual in connection with labor services
      rendered commits:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 30. Human Trafficking › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3019. Victim protection during prosecution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3019. Victim protection during prosecution (2023)
content:
(a) Disclosure of name of victim of human trafficking.--Notwithstanding any other provision of law to the contrary, unless the court otherwise
      orders in a prosecution involving a victim of human trafficking, an officer or employee
      of the court may not disclose the identity of the victim of human trafficking to the
      public.  Any record revealing the name of the victim of human trafficking shall not be open
      to public inspection.

content:
The Pennsylvania Commission on Sentencing established in42 Pa.C.S. § 2151.2(relating to commission) shall collect data and other relevant information on sentences
   imposed under this subchapter.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3052. Protection of victims (2023)
content:
Law enforcement agencies shall take reasonable steps necessary to identify, protect
   and assist victims of human trafficking.

content:
(a) Suspension of professional license.--The professional license of a licensee who in the course of a violation of this chapter
      knowingly employs or permits the employment of a victim of human trafficking shall
      be suspended for a minimum period of one year.

content:
Any remedies under this chapter shall be in addition to any other criminal penalties
   or forfeitures authorized under the laws of this Commonwealth.

content:
(a) Voluntary placement.--Residence of a victim of human trafficking in a shelter or other facility shall be
      voluntary, and a victim of human trafficking may decline to stay in a shelter or other
      facility.

      special relief.

   concurrent authority to investigate and institute criminal proceedings under the provisions

   enhancements for courts to consider in cases involving trafficking in individuals
   and involuntary servitude.

   the provision of specialized services to sexually exploited children.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 30. Human Trafficking›Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3072. Nonexclusivity

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3072. Nonexclusivity (2023)
content:
Remedies under this chapter are not exclusive and shall be in addition to other procedures
   or remedies for a violation or conduct provided for in other law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Chapter 30. Human Trafficking›Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3071. Funding
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Chapter 30. Human Trafficking › Subchapter E. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3071. Funding
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3071. Funding (2023)
content:
In addition to any money that may be appropriated from time to time by the General
   Assembly for its work, the commission may apply for and expend Federal grants and
   grants and contributions from other public, quasi-public or private sources to assist
   in implementing this chapter.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3012. Involuntary servitude
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3012. Involuntary servitude
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3012. Involuntary servitude (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person commits a felony of the first degree if the person knowingly, through any
      of the means described in subsection (b), subjects an individual to labor servitude
      or sexual servitude, except where the conduct is permissible under Federal or State
      law other than this chapter.

content:
(a) Safe harbor.--If it is determined by a law enforcement officer, after reasonable detention for investigative
      purposes, that an individual is under 18 years of age and is determined to be a sexually
      exploited child as defined in section 3001 (relating to definitions), the individual
      shall be immune from:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3016. Obstruction of justice

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3016. Obstruction of justice (2023)
content:
A person who commits a violation of Subchapter B of Chapter 49 (relating to victim
   and witness intimidation)1or Chapter 51 (relating to obstructing governmental operations) that in any way interferes
   with or prevents the enforcement of this chapter shall be subject to the same penalties
   that may be imposed for the offense for which the person has been charged under this
   chapter.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3018. Evidence and defenses to human trafficking
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3018. Evidence and defenses to human trafficking (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Evidence of the age of the victim of human trafficking with respect to the age of
      consent to sex or legal age of marriage shall not constitute a defense in a prosecution
      for a violation under this chapter, nor shall the evidence preclude a finding of a
      violation under this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3019. Victim protection during prosecution
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3019. Victim protection during prosecution
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3019. Victim protection during prosecution (2023)
content:
(a) Disclosure of name of victim of human trafficking.--Notwithstanding any other provision of law to the contrary, unless the court otherwise
      orders in a prosecution involving a victim of human trafficking, an officer or employee
      of the court may not disclose the identity of the victim of human trafficking to the
      public.  Any record revealing the name of the victim of human trafficking shall not be open
      to public inspection.

content:
In addition to the provisions of section 1106 (relating to restitution for injuries
   to person or property), the following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3022. Professional licenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3022. Professional licenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3022. Professional licenses (2023)
content:
(a) Suspension of professional license.--The professional license of a licensee who in the course of a violation of this chapter
      knowingly employs or permits the employment of a victim of human trafficking shall
      be suspended for a minimum period of one year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3024. Sentencing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3024. Sentencing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3024. Sentencing (2023)
content:
The Pennsylvania Commission on Sentencing, in accordance with42 Pa.C.S. § 2154(relating to adoption of guidelines for sentencing), shall provide for sentencing
   enhancements for courts to consider in cases involving trafficking in individuals
   and involuntary servitude.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3026. Concurrent jurisdiction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3026. Concurrent jurisdiction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3026. Concurrent jurisdiction (2023)
content:
The Attorney General and the district attorneys of the several counties shall have
   concurrent authority to investigate and institute criminal proceedings under the provisions
   of this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 23. General Provisions›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2301. Definitions

   following words and phrases, when used in this article shall have, unless the context

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3023. Cumulative remedies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3023. Cumulative remedies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3023. Cumulative remedies (2023)
content:
Any remedies under this chapter shall be in addition to any other criminal penalties
   or forfeitures authorized under the laws of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504. Involuntary manslaughter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504. Involuntary manslaughter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2504. Involuntary manslaughter (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person is guilty of involuntary manslaughter when as a direct result of the doing
      of an unlawful act in a reckless or grossly negligent manner, or the doing of a lawful
      act in a reckless or grossly negligent manner, he causes the death of another person.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person›Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3025. Data collection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Article B. Offenses Involving Danger to the Person › Subchapter B. Prosecution of Human Trafficking › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3025. Data collection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 3025. Data collection (2023)
content:
The Pennsylvania Commission on Sentencing established in42 Pa.C.S. § 2151.2(relating to commission) shall collect data and other relevant information on sentences
   imposed under this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Murder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Murder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Murder (2023)
content:
(a) Murder of the first degree.--A criminal homicide constitutes murder of the first degree when it is committed by
      an intentional killing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Criminal homicide
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Criminal homicide
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Criminal homicide (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person is guilty of criminal homicide if he intentionally, knowingly, recklessly
      or negligently causes the death of another human being.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Voluntary manslaughter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Voluntary manslaughter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Voluntary manslaughter (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person who kills an individual without lawful justification commits voluntary
      manslaughter if at the time of the killing he is acting under a sudden and intense
      passion resulting from serious provocation by:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Drug delivery resulting in death
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Drug delivery resulting in death
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Drug delivery resulting in death (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person commits a felony of the first degree if the person intentionally administers,
      dispenses, delivers, gives, prescribes, sells or distributes any controlled substance
      or counterfeit controlled substance in violation of section 13(a)(14) or (30) of the
      act of April 14, 1972 (P.L. 233, No. 64),1known as The Controlled Substance, Drug, Device and Cosmetic Act, and another person
      dies as a result of using the substance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 26. Crimes Against Unborn Child›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2603. Criminal homicide of unborn child
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 26. Crimes Against Unborn Child › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2603. Criminal homicide of unborn child
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2603. Criminal homicide of unborn child (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--An individual commits criminal homicide of an unborn child if the individual intentionally,
      knowingly, recklessly or negligently causes the death of an unborn child in violation
      of section 2604 (relating to murder of unborn child) or 2605 (relating to voluntary
      manslaughter of unborn child).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Causing or aiding suicide
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 25. Criminal Homicide › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Causing or aiding suicide
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2505. Causing or aiding suicide (2023)
content:
(a) Causing suicide as criminal homicide.--A person may be convicted of criminal homicide for causing another to die by suicide
      only if he intentionally causes such suicide by force, duress or deception.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 26. Crimes Against Unborn Child›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2601. Short title of chapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 26. Crimes Against Unborn Child › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2601. Short title of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2601. Short title of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the Crimes Against the Unborn Child

(a) Murder of a law enforcement officer of the first degree.--A person commits murder of a law enforcement officer of the first degree who intentionally

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2606. Aggravated assault of unborn child (2023)
content:
(a) Offense.--A person commits aggravated assault of an unborn child if he attempts to cause serious
      bodily injury to the unborn child or causes such injury intentionally, knowingly or
      recklessly under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to the life of the
      unborn child.

      into a vehicle or instrumentality of public transportation that is occupied by one
      or more persons commits a misdemeanor of the first degree.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 27. Assault › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2703.1. Aggravated harassment by prisoner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2703.1. Aggravated harassment by prisoner (2023)
content:
A person who is confined in or committed to any local or county detention facility,
   jail or prison or any State penal or correctional institution or other State penal
   or correctional facility located in this Commonwealth commits a felony of the third
   degree if he, while so confined or committed or while undergoing transportation to
   or from such an institution or facility in or to which he was confined or committed,
   intentionally or knowingly causes or attempts to cause another to come into contact
   with blood, seminal fluid, saliva, urine or feces by throwing, tossing, spitting or
   expelling such fluid or material.

content:

      of the first degree if he uses or directs the use of tear or noxious gas against any

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2712. Assault on sports official (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person who violates section 2701 (relating to simple assault), where the victim
      is a sports official who was assaulted during a sports event or was assaulted as a
      result of his or her official acts as a sports official, is guilty of assault on a
      sports official.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 27. Assault›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2710. Ethnic intimidation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 27. Assault › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2710. Ethnic intimidation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2710. Ethnic intimidation (2023)
content:
(a) Offense defined.--A person commits the offense of ethnic intimidation if, with malicious intention toward
      the race, color, religion or national origin of another individual or group of individuals,
      he commits an offense under any other provision of this article or under Chapter 33
      (relating to arson, criminal mischief and other property destruction) exclusive of
      section 3307 (relating to institutional vandalism) or under section 3503 (relating
      to criminal trespass) with respect to such individual or his or her property or with
      respect to one or more members of such group or to their property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses›Chapter 27. Assault›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2711. Probable cause arrests in domestic violence cases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 27. Assault › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2711. Probable cause arrests in domestic violence cases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2711. Probable cause arrests in domestic violence cases (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A police officer shall have the same right of arrest without a warrant as in a felony
      whenever he has probable cause to believe the defendant has violated section 2504
      (relating to involuntary manslaughter), 2701 (relating to simple assault), 2702(a)(3),
      (4) and (5) (relating to aggravated assault), 2705 (relating to recklessly endangering
      another person), 2706 (relating to terroristic threats), 2709.1 (relating to stalking)
      or 2718 (relating to strangulation) against a family or household member although
      the offense did not take place in the presence of the police officer.  A police officer may not arrest a person pursuant to this section without first
      observing recent physical injury to the victim or other corroborative evidence.  For the purposes of this subsection, the term “family or household member” has the meaning given that term in23 Pa.C.S. § 6102(relating to definitions).

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part II. Definition of Specific Offenses › Chapter 27. Assault › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2714. Unauthorized administration of intoxicant
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 2714. Unauthorized administration of intoxicant (2023)
content:
A person commits a felony of the third degree when, with the intent to commit an offense
   under section 3121(a)(4) (relating to rape), 3123(a)(4) (relating to involuntary deviate
   sexual intercourse), 3125(5) (relating to aggravated indecent assault) or 3126(a)(5)
   (relating to indecent assault), he or she substantially impairs the complainant's
   power to appraise or control his or her conduct by administering, without the knowledge
   of the complainant, drugs or other intoxicants.

content:

      knowingly or recklessly possesses or manufactures a weapon of mass destruction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9105. Other criminal justice information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9105. Other criminal justice information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9105. Other criminal justice information (2023)
content:
Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to apply to information concerning juveniles,
   except as provided in section 9123 (relating to juvenile records), unless they have
   been adjudicated as adults, nor shall it apply to intelligence information, investigative
   information, treatment information, including medical and psychiatric information,
   caution indicator information, modus operandi information, wanted persons information,
   stolen property information, missing persons information, employment history information,
   personal history information, nor presentence investigation information.  Criminal history record information maintained as a part of these records shall
   not be disseminated unless in compliance with the provisions of this chapter.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter B. Completeness and Accuracy › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9111. Duties of criminal justice agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9111. Duties of criminal justice agencies (2023)
content:
It shall be the duty of every criminal justice agency within the Commonwealth to maintain
   complete and accurate criminal history record information and to report such information
   at such times and in such manner as required by the provisions of this chapter or
   other applicable statutes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter B. Completeness and Accuracy›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9112. Mandatory fingerprinting
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter B. Completeness and Accuracy › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9112. Mandatory fingerprinting
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9112. Mandatory fingerprinting (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Fingerprints of all persons arrested for a felony, misdemeanor or summary offense
      which becomes a misdemeanor on a second arrest after conviction of that summary offense,
      shall be taken by the arresting authority, and within 48 hours of the arrest, shall
      be forwarded to, and in a manner and such a form as provided by, the central repository.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter C. Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9121. General regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter C. Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9121. General regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9121. General regulations (2023)
content:
(a) Dissemination to criminal justice agencies.--Criminal history record information maintained by any criminal justice agency shall
      be disseminated without charge to any criminal justice agency or to any noncriminal
      justice agency that is providing a service for which a criminal justice agency is
      responsible.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter B. Completeness and Accuracy›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9113. Disposition reporting by criminal justice agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter B. Completeness and Accuracy › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9113. Disposition reporting by criminal justice agencies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9113. Disposition reporting by criminal justice agencies (2023)
content:
(a) Reports of dispositions required.--All criminal justice agencies, including but not limited to, courts, county, regional
      and State correctional institutions and parole and probation agencies, shall collect
      and submit reports of dispositions occurring within their respective agencies for
      criminal history record information, within 90 days of the date of such disposition
      to the central repository as provided for in this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9106. Information in central repository or automated systems
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9106. Information in central repository or automated systems
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9106. Information in central repository or automated systems (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Intelligence information, investigative information and treatment information shall
      not be collected in the central repository.  This prohibition shall not preclude the collection in the central repository of
      names, words, numbers, phrases or other similar index keys to serve as indices to
      investigative reports.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter C. Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9122.6. Employer immunity from liability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter C. Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9122.6. Employer immunity from liability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9122.6. Employer immunity from liability (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An employer who employs or otherwise engages an individual whose criminal history
      record has been expunged or to which limited access has been applied under section
      9122.1 (relating to petition for limited access) or 9122.2 (relating to clean slate
      limited access) shall be immune from liability for any claim arising out of the misconduct
      of the individual, if the misconduct relates to the portion of the criminal history
      record that has been expunged or provided limited access.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter C. Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9122.1. Petition for limited access
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter C. Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9122.1. Petition for limited access
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9122.1. Petition for limited access (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to the exceptions in subsection (b) and notwithstanding any other provision
      of this chapter, upon petition of a person who has been free from conviction for a
      period of seven years for an offense punishable by one or more years in prison and
      has completed payment of all court-ordered restitution and the fee previously authorized
      to carry out the limited access and clean slate limited access provisions, the court
      of common pleas in the jurisdiction where a conviction occurred may enter an order
      that criminal history record information maintained by a criminal justice agency pertaining
      to a qualifying misdemeanor or an ungraded offense which carries a maximum penalty
      of no more than five years be disseminated only to a criminal justice agency or as
      provided in section 9121(b.1) and (b.2) (relating to general regulations).  A court may not enter an order under this subsection unless the person who filed
      the petition, upon payment of all court-ordered restitution, also paid the fee previously
      authorized to carry out the limited access and clean slate limited access provisions.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9122.4. Order to vacate order for limited access (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Upon petition of the prosecuting attorney to the court where a conviction occurred,
      and with notice to the defendant and opportunity to be heard, the court shall vacate
      an order for limited access granted under section 9122.2 (relating to clean slate
      limited access) if the court determines that the order was erroneously entered and
      not in accordance with section 9122.2.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter C. Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9124. Use of records by licensing agencies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter C. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9124. Use of records by licensing agencies (2023)
content:
(a) State agencies.--Except as provided by this chapter and specifically subsection (a.1), a board, commission
      or department of the Commonwealth, when determining eligibility for licensing, certification,
      registration or permission to engage in a trade, profession or occupation, may consider
      convictions of the applicant of crimes but the convictions shall not preclude the
      issuance of a license, certificate, registration or permit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter E. Audit›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9142. Quality control

content:
Each repository shall establish effective procedures, in compliance with rules and
   regulations promulgated by the Attorney General, for the completeness and accuracy
   of criminal history record information.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter E. Audit › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9143. Regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9143. Regulations (2023)
content:

   the Pennsylvania State Police, to adopt rules and regulations pursuant to this act.  The Office of Attorney General, in consultation with the Pennsylvania State Police,
   shall have the power and authority to promulgate, adopt, publish and use guidelines

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter F. Individual Right of Access and Review›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9153. Individual rights on access and review
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter F. Individual Right of Access and Review › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9153. Individual rights on access and review
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9153. Individual rights on access and review (2023)
content:
Any individual exercising his or her right to access and review under the provisions
   of this subchapter shall be informed when criminal history record information is made
   available that he or she is under no obligation to divulge such information to any
   person or agency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter C. Dissemination of Criminal History Record Information›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9125. Use of records for employment

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9125. Use of records for employment (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Whenever an employer is in receipt of information which is part of an employment applicant's
      criminal history record information file, it may use that information for the purpose
      of deciding whether or not to hire the applicant, only in accordance with this section.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter F.1. Crime Victim Right of Access › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9158.1. Right to access

   history investigative information under this subchapter for use in or investigation
   of an actual or potential civil action in this Commonwealth relating to that criminal
   history investigative information.

Repositories maintaining criminal history record information shall inform the public
   and post in a public place, notice of the existence, purpose, use and accessibility
   of the criminal history record information they maintain and the requirements of the
   repository for identification on individual access and review.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information › Subchapter I. Sanctions › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9183. Civil actions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9183. Civil actions (2023)
content:
(a) Injunctions.--The Attorney General or any other individual or agency may institute an action in
      a court of proper jurisdiction against any person, agency or organization to enjoin
      any criminal justice agency, noncriminal justice agency, organization or individual
      violating the provisions of this chapter or to compel such agency, organization or
      person to comply with the provisions of this chapter.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9101. Short title of chapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9101. Short title of chapter (2023)
content:
This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Criminal History Record Information
   Act.”

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9158.5. Protection of information (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Nothing under this subchapter shall be construed to permit the dissemination of otherwise

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9103. Applicability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses › Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9103. Applicability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9103. Applicability (2023)
content:
This chapter shall apply to persons within this Commonwealth and to any agency of
   the Commonwealth or its political subdivisions which collects, maintains, disseminates
   or receives criminal history record information.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 18 Pa.C.S.A. Crimes and Offenses›Part III. Miscellaneous Provisions›Chapter 91. Criminal History Record Information›Subchapter F.1. Crime Victim Right of Access›PA ST 18 Pa.C.S.A. § 9158.6. Current dissemination not limited

content:
